sentences.zh: 羅亨信，字用實，東莞人。

translations.literal: Luo Hengxin, style name Yongshi, was a man of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Hengxin, whose style was Yongshi, came from Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Yongle reign.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Yongle 2 (1404).

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授工科給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to junior compiler and appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Hanlin junior compiler, then appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 出視浙江水災，奏蠲三縣租。

translations.literal: Sent out to inspect the flood disaster in Zhejiang, he memorialized to remit the land tax of three counties.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatched to inspect flooding in Zhejiang, he secured remission of land tax for three counties.

sentences.zh: 進吏科右給事中，坐累謫交阯為吏。

translations.literal: Promoted to right supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, he was implicated in a case and demoted to Jiaozhi as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to right supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, he was caught up in a case and banished to Jiaozhi as a lowly clerk.

sentences.zh: 居九年，仁宗嗣位，始召入為御史。

translations.literal: After nine years there, when the Renzong Emperor succeeded to the throne, he was at last summoned back as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: Nine years later, when the Renzong Emperor came to the throne, he was finally recalled and made a censor.

sentences.zh: 核通州倉儲，巡按畿內，清軍山西，皆有聲。

translations.literal: Auditing Tongzhou granary stores, touring as investigating censor within the capital region, and inspecting troops in Shanxi, he won renown in each post.
translations.idiomatic: Whether auditing Tongzhou's granaries, investigating the capital region, or inspecting troops in Shanxi, he earned a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 宣德中，有薦其堪方面者。

translations.literal: In the Xuande era someone recommended him as fit for a regional post.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuande reign someone recommended him for provincial office.

sentences.zh: 命食按察僉事俸，待遷。

translations.literal: He was ordered to draw the salary of an assistant surveillance commissioner while awaiting transfer.
translations.idiomatic: He was given an assistant surveillance commissioner's salary pending appointment.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位之三月，擢右僉都御史，練兵平涼、西寧。

translations.literal: In the third month after the Yingzong Emperor's accession he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief on the right and drilled troops at Pingliang and Xining.
translations.idiomatic: Three months after the Yingzong Emperor took the throne, he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief on the right and put in charge of training troops at Pingliang and Xining.

sentences.zh: 正統二年，蔣貴討阿臺、朵兒只伯，亨信參其軍務。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengtong, Jiang Gui campaigned against Atai and Duo'erzhibo, and Hengxin took part in the military planning.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 2 (1437), when Jiang Gui marched against Atai and Duo'erzhibo, Hengxin joined the campaign staff.

sentences.zh: 至魚兒海，貴等以芻餉不繼，留十日引還。

translations.literal: Reaching Yurhai, Gui and the others, because fodder and provisions did not keep up, stayed ten days and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At Yurhai, Gui and his commanders halted ten days for lack of fodder and supplies, then turned back.

sentences.zh: 亨信讓之曰：「公等受國厚恩，敢臨敵退縮耶？

translations.literal: Hengxin reproached them, saying: You gentlemen have received thick favor from the state—how dare you shrink back before the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: Hengxin rebuked them: "You have received great favor from the state—how dare you flinch before the enemy?

sentences.zh: 死法孰與死敵？」

translations.literal: Which is worse, to die by law or to die fighting the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: Is it better to die by the law or die facing the foe?"

sentences.zh: 貴不從。

translations.literal: Gui did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui would not listen.

sentences.zh: 亨信上章言貴逗遛狀。

translations.literal: Hengxin submitted a memorial describing Gui's procrastination.
translations.idiomatic: Hengxin memorialized the throne reporting Gui's delay and withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 帝以其章示監督尚書王驥等。

translations.literal: The Emperor showed his memorial to the supervising minister Wang Ji and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor showed the memorial to the supervising minister Wang Ji and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 明年進兵，大破之。

translations.literal: The next year the army advanced and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the army advanced and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 亨信以參贊功，進秩一等。

translations.literal: Hengxin, for his merit as campaign adviser, was promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: For his service on the campaign staff, Hengxin was promoted one grade.

sentences.zh: 父喪歸葬。

translations.literal: On his father's death he returned home for the burial.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he went home to observe mourning and bury him.

sentences.zh: 還朝，改命巡撫宣府、大同。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he was reassigned to serve as grand coordinator of Xuanfu and Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he was reassigned as grand coordinator of Xuanfu and Datong.

sentences.zh: 參將石亨請簡大同民三之一為軍，亨信奏止之。

translations.literal: The assistant commander Shi Heng requested that one-third of Datong's civilians be selected as soldiers; Hengxin memorialized to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant commander Shi Heng asked to draft one-third of Datong's civilians into the army; Hengxin memorialized and blocked the plan.

sentences.zh: 十年進右副都御史，巡撫如故。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief on the right, continuing as grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief on the right while retaining his coordinating duties.

sentences.zh: 時遣官度二鎮軍田，一軍八十畝外，悉征稅五升。

translations.literal: At the time officials were sent to survey military fields in the two garrisons; beyond eighty mu per soldier, all was taxed at five sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were then sent to measure military farmland in both garrisons, with a tax of five sheng levied on everything above eighty mu per soldier.

sentences.zh: 亨信言：「文皇帝時，詔邊軍盡力墾田，毋征稅，陛下復申命之。

translations.literal: Hengxin said: In the time of the Wenzong Emperor an edict ordered border troops to farm with all their strength and forbade taxation; Your Majesty has reiterated that command.
translations.idiomatic: Hengxin said: "Under the Hongwu Emperor, border troops were ordered to farm to the full and pay no tax, and Your Majesty has reaffirmed that policy.

sentences.zh: 今奈何忽為此舉？

translations.literal: Why now suddenly take this step?
translations.idiomatic: Why suddenly do this now?

sentences.zh: 塞上諸軍，防邊勞苦，無他生業，惟事田作。

translations.literal: The troops on the frontier, laboring hard in border defense, have no other livelihood and rely solely on farming.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier soldiers endure harsh border duty and have no other livelihood—they live only by the plow.

sentences.zh: 每歲自冬徂春，迎送瓦剌使臣，三月始得就田，七月又復刈草，八月以後，修治關塞，計一歲中曾無休暇。

translations.literal: Every year from winter through spring they escort Oirat envoys; only in the third month can they take to the fields; in the seventh month they cut grass again, and from the eighth month onward they repair passes and fortifications—in a whole year they scarcely have a moment's rest.
translations.idiomatic: Each year from winter into spring they escort Oirat envoys; they cannot reach the fields until the third month, must cut fodder again in the seventh, and from the eighth month on repair passes and walls—in all, they have almost no leisure in a year.

sentences.zh: 況邊地磽瘠，霜早收薄，若更征稅，則民不復井，必致竄逸。

translations.literal: Moreover the borderlands are barren and thin; frost comes early and harvests are meager—if tax is levied again, the people will not return to their fields and will surely flee and scatter.
translations.idiomatic: The border country is poor and thin-soiled, with early frost and scant harvests; further taxation would drive people from their farms and send them fleeing.

sentences.zh: 計臣但務積粟，不知人心不固，雖有粟，將誰與守？」

translations.literal: Your planners seek only to pile up grain, not knowing that if hearts are not secure, though there be grain, who will guard it?
translations.idiomatic: Your planners care only to hoard grain, not seeing that if the people are unsettled, grain alone will not hold the frontier—who will defend it?"

sentences.zh: 帝納其言而止。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted his words and stopped the measure.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted his advice and halted the levy.

sentences.zh: 初，亨信嘗奏言：「也先專候釁端，以圖入寇。

translations.literal: Earlier Hengxin had memorialized: Esen watches constantly for an opening to invade.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Hengxin had warned: "Esen waits only for a pretext to raid.

sentences.zh: 宜預於直北要害，增置城衛為備。

translations.literal: We should beforehand at key points due north of the capital add walled garrisons as a precaution.
translations.idiomatic: We should strengthen walled garrisons at the vital passes north of the capital before he strikes.

sentences.zh: 不然，恐貽大患。」

translations.literal: Otherwise I fear a great calamity will be left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise we risk grave harm."

sentences.zh: 兵部議，寢不行。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War deliberated and the proposal was shelved and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War discussed it, and the plan was shelved.

sentences.zh: 及土木之變，人情洶懼。

translations.literal: When the Tumu disaster occurred, popular feeling was turbulent with fear.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tumu disaster panic spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 有議棄宣府城者，官吏軍民紛然爭出。

translations.literal: Some proposed abandoning Xuanfu city; officials, soldiers, and civilians all scrambled to get out.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged abandoning Xuanfu; officials, troops, and townspeople rushed to flee.

sentences.zh: 亨信仗劍坐城下，令曰：「出城者斬！」

translations.literal: Hengxin, sword in hand, sat below the wall and ordered: Whoever leaves the city shall be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: Hengxin sat below the wall with his sword drawn and proclaimed: "Whoever leaves the city dies!"

sentences.zh: 又誓諸將為朝廷死守，人心始定。

translations.literal: He also swore the generals to die holding the city for the court, and hearts were steadied.
translations.idiomatic: He then bound his officers by oath to hold the city for the throne, and morale steadied.

sentences.zh: 也先挾上皇至城南，傳命啟門。

translations.literal: Esen, holding the captured emperor, came to the south of the city and sent word ordering the gates opened.
translations.idiomatic: Esen brought the captive emperor to the south wall and demanded the gates be opened.

sentences.zh: 亨信登城語曰：「奉命守城，不敢擅啟。」

translations.literal: Hengxin mounted the wall and said: I have orders to hold the city and dare not open the gates on my own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Hengxin mounted the wall and replied: "I am under orders to defend the city and dare not open the gates without command."

sentences.zh: 也先逡巡引去。

translations.literal: Esen hesitated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Esen lingered, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 赤城、雕鶚、懷來、永寧、保安諸守將棄城遁，並按其罪。

translations.literal: The defending generals at Chicheng, Diaoe, Huailai, Yongning, and Bao'an abandoned their cities and fled; he prosecuted them all.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commanders at Chicheng, Diaoe, Huailai, Yongning, and Bao'an had abandoned their posts; he had them all punished.

sentences.zh: 侯琎。

translations.literal: Hou Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jin.

sentences.zh: 字廷玉。

translations.literal: Style name Tingyu.
translations.idiomatic: His style was Tingyu.

sentences.zh: 澤州人。

translations.literal: A man of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was a native of Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 少慷慨有誌節。

translations.literal: In youth he was generous and possessed resolve and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was openhanded and firm in purpose.

sentences.zh: 登宣德二年進士，授行人。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the second year of Xuande and was appointed courier.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in Xuande 2 (1427) and was made a courier.

sentences.zh: 烏撒、烏蒙土官以爭地相仇殺，詔遣琎及同官章聰諭解之，正其疆理而還。

translations.literal: The native officials of Wusa and Wumeng were killing one another over disputed land; an edict sent Jin and his colleague Zhang Cong to instruct and settle them, and they rectified the boundaries and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Native chiefs of Wusa and Wumeng were feuding over territory; the court sent Jin and Zhang Cong to mediate, fix the borders, and return.

sentences.zh: 副侍郎章敞使交阯，關門卑，前驅傴而入，琎叱曰：「此狗竇耳，奈何辱天使！」

translations.literal: Vice minister Zhang Chang was envoy to Jiaozhi; the gate was low and the outriders stooped to enter; Jin shouted: This is a dog hole—how can you insult the imperial envoy!
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Minister Zhang Chang went to Jiaozhi, the gate was so low his escort had to stoop; Jin cried out: "This is a dog hole—how dare you humiliate the emperor's envoy!"

sentences.zh: 交人為毀關，乃入。

translations.literal: The people of Jiaozhi tore down the gate, and only then did they enter.
translations.idiomatic: The Annamese tore the gate down before they would enter.

sentences.zh: 及歸，饋遺無所受。

translations.literal: On returning he accepted none of the gifts offered.
translations.idiomatic: On the way home he refused every gift offered him.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部主事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to secretary in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to secretary in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 正統初，從尚書柴車等出鐵門關禦阿臺有功，進郎中。

translations.literal: At the start of Zhengtong he followed Minister Chai Che and others through Iron Gate Pass to repel Atai with merit and was promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengtong he served under Minister Chai Che at Iron Gate Pass against Atai with distinction and was made a director.

sentences.zh: 從王驥征麓川，至金齒。

translations.literal: He followed Wang Ji in the campaign against Luchuan and reached Jingchi.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Wang Ji's Luchuan campaign as far as Jingchi.

sentences.zh: 驥自統大軍擊思任發，而遣琎援大侯州。

translations.literal: Ji himself led the main army against Si Renfa while sending Jin to relieve Dahu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ji led the main force against Si Renfa while dispatching Jin to relieve Dahu.

sentences.zh: 賊眾三萬至，督都指揮馬讓、盧鉞擊走之。

translations.literal: Thirty thousand bandits arrived; he supervised regional commanders Ma Rang and Lu Yue in driving them off.
translations.idiomatic: When thirty thousand rebels arrived, he directed regional commanders Ma Rang and Lu Yue to beat them back.

sentences.zh: 遂由高黎貢山兼程夜行，會大軍，壓其巢。

translations.literal: Then by forced marches by night over the Gaoligong Mountains he joined the main army and pressed their stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched day and night over the Gaoligong range, joined the main army, and pressed the enemy's lair.

sentences.zh: 麓川平，拜禮部右侍郎，參贊雲南軍務，詔與楊寧二年更代。

translations.literal: When Luchuan was pacified he was appointed vice minister of rites on the right and adviser on Yunnan military affairs, with an edict that he and Yang Ning rotate every two years.
translations.idiomatic: After Luchuan was pacified he became vice minister of rites and military adviser in Yunnan, with orders to rotate with Yang Ning every two years.

sentences.zh: 驥再征麓川。

translations.literal: Ji campaigned against Luchuan again.
translations.idiomatic: Ji campaigned in Luchuan a second time.

sentences.zh: 琎以功遷左。

translations.literal: Jin was transferred to the left for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: For his service Jin was moved to the left-hand vice ministership.

sentences.zh: 九年代還。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he rotated home.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he returned on rotation.

sentences.zh: 母憂，起復，尋調兵部。

translations.literal: During mourning for his mother he was recalled to service and soon transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he was recalled from mourning and soon moved to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 十一年復代寧鎮雲南。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he again replaced Ning in commanding Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he again relieved Ning as commander in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 思機發竄孟養，驥復南征。

translations.literal: Si Jifa fled to Mengyang; Ji marched south again.
translations.idiomatic: Si Jifa had fled to Mengyang, and Ji marched south once more.

sentences.zh: 琎與都督張軏分兵進抵金沙江，破之鬼哭山。

translations.literal: Jin and regional commander Zhang Ruan advanced in separate columns to the Jinsha River and defeated the enemy at Guikushan.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and regional commander Zhang Ruan advanced in separate columns to the Jinsha River and routed the enemy at Ghost-Weeping Mountain.

sentences.zh: 璽書褒賚。

translations.literal: An imperial letter praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial letter praised and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，貴州苗韋同烈叛，圍新添、平越、清平、興隆諸衛。

translations.literal: At the start of Jingtai the Miao chieftain Wei Tonglie of Guizhou rebelled and besieged the guards of Xintian, Pingyue, Qingping, and Xinglong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingtai reign the Guizhou Miao leader Wei Tonglie rebelled and besieged the guards of Xintian, Pingyue, Qingping, and Xinglong.

sentences.zh: 命琎總督貴州軍務討之。

translations.literal: Jin was ordered to take overall command of Guizhou military affairs to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was ordered to take overall command in Guizhou and suppress the revolt.

sentences.zh: 時副總兵田禮巳解新添、平越圍，琎遂遣兵攻敗都盧、水西諸賊，貴州道始通。

translations.literal: By then vice commander Tian Li had already lifted the sieges of Xintian and Pingyue; Jin then sent troops to defeat the bandits of Dulou, Shuixi, and elsewhere, and the Guizhou routes were opened.
translations.idiomatic: Vice commander Tian Li had already relieved Xintian and Pingyue; Jin then sent troops to defeat the rebels of Dulou and Shuixi, and the roads through Guizhou were cleared.

sentences.zh: 又調雲南兵，由烏撒會師，開畢節諸路，檄普安土兵援安南衛，而自率師攻紫塘、彌勒等十余寨。

translations.literal: He also shifted Yunnan troops, joined forces via Wusa, opened the routes through Bijie, ordered native troops of Pu'an to relieve Annan Guard, and himself led the army against more than ten stockades including Zitang and Mile.
translations.idiomatic: He brought up Yunnan troops, united them at Wusa, opened the Bijie routes, called Pu'an native levies to relieve Annan Guard, and personally attacked more than ten strongholds including Zitang and Mile.

sentences.zh: 會賊復圍平越，回師擊退之。

translations.literal: When the bandits again besieged Pingyue he turned his army back and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels again besieged Pingyue he wheeled about and repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 遂分哨七盤坡、羊腸河、楊老堡，解清平圍，東至重安江，與驥兵會。

translations.literal: He then detached columns to Qipanpo, Yangchang River, and Yanglaobao, lifted the siege of Qingping, and marched east to the Chong'an River, where he joined Wang Ji's forces.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent detachments to Qipanpo, Yangchang River, and Yanglaobao, relieved Qingping, and marched east to the Chong'an River to join Wang Ji.

sentences.zh: 興隆抵鎮遠道皆通。

translations.literal: The routes from Xinglong to Zhenyuan were all opened.
translations.idiomatic: The road from Xinglong to Zhenyuan was fully open.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，進兵部尚書。

translations.literal: On report of victory he was promoted to minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: Victory reported, he was made minister of war.

sentences.zh: 進克賞改苗，擒其渠王阿同等三十四人。

translations.literal: Advancing he overcame the Shanggai Miao and captured their leader Wang Atong and thirty-four others.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced against the Shanggai Miao and captured their chieftain Wang Atong and thirty-four others.

sentences.zh: 別賊阿趙偽稱趙王，率眾掠清平，琎復討擒之。

translations.literal: Another bandit, A Zhao, falsely styled himself Prince of Zhao, led a host to plunder Qingping, and Jin again campaigned and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Another rebel, A Zhao, styled himself Prince Zhao and raided Qingping; Jin campaigned again and took him.

sentences.zh: 水西苗阿忽等六族皆自乞歸化，詔琎隨方處置。

translations.literal: The six tribes of the Shuixi Miao led by A Hu all begged on their own to submit; an edict ordered Jin to settle them as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Six Shuixi Miao tribes led by A Hu all offered submission; the court ordered Jin to settle them as local conditions allowed.

sentences.zh: 楊寧，字彥謐，歙人。

translations.literal: Yang Ning, style name Yanmi, was a man of She County.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ning, whose style was Yanmi, came from She County.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fifth year of Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Xuande 5 (1430).

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事。

translations.literal: Appointed secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 機警多才能，負時譽。

translations.literal: Alert and gifted with many talents, he enjoyed the reputation of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and widely capable, he enjoyed a strong contemporary reputation.

sentences.zh: 正統初，從尚書魏源巡視宣、大。

translations.literal: At the start of Zhengtong he followed Minister Wei Yuan in inspecting Xuanfu and Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengtong he joined Minister Wei Yuan on an inspection tour of Xuanfu and Datong.

sentences.zh: 四年與都督吳亮征麓川。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he campaigned against Luchuan with regional commander Wu Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he campaigned in Luchuan with regional commander Wu Liang.

sentences.zh: 賊款軍門約降，寧曰：「兵未加而先降，誘我也，宜嚴兵待之。」

translations.literal: The bandits came to the camp gate offering surrender; Ning said: If they surrender before we have struck, they are luring us—we should keep the army on strict alert.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came to camp offering surrender; Ning said, "They are surrendering before we have even fought—this is a trap. Keep the army on full alert."

sentences.zh: 不聽，令寧督運金齒。

translations.literal: They did not listen and ordered Ning to supervise transport to Jingchi.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was ignored, and Ning was ordered to supervise supplies to Jingchi.

sentences.zh: 已而賊果大至，官兵敗績。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits did arrive in force and the government troops suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels came in force and the army was routed.

sentences.zh: 諸將獲罪，寧擢郎中。

translations.literal: The generals were punished, but Ning was promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: The generals were punished while Ning was promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 復從王驥至騰沖破賊，寧與太仆少卿李蕡督戰，並有功。

translations.literal: He again followed Wang Ji to Tengchong and defeated the bandits; Ning and Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud Li Fen supervised the fighting, and both had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Wang Ji to Tengchong, where Ning and Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud Li Fen directed the fighting; both were credited with merit.

sentences.zh: 師還，寧超拜刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Ning was exceptionally appointed vice minister of justice on the right.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return Ning was exceptionally promoted to vice minister of justice on the right.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，奪情。

translations.literal: On his mother's death he was recalled from mourning to serve.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he was recalled from mourning to duty.

sentences.zh: 九年代侯琎參贊雲南軍務。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he replaced Hou Jin as adviser on Yunnan military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he relieved Hou Jin as military adviser in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 時麓川甫平，寧以騰沖地要害，與都督沐昂築城置衛，設戍兵控諸蠻。

translations.literal: Luchuan had just been pacified; Ning, because Tengchong was strategically vital, with regional commander Mu Ang built a walled city and established a guard, posting garrison troops to control the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Luchuan had just been pacified; judging Tengchong vital, Ning and regional commander Mu Ang built a walled city, established a guard, and posted troops to hold the tribes in check.

sentences.zh: 邊方遂定。

translations.literal: The frontier was thus settled.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier was thus stabilized.

sentences.zh: 居二年，召還。

translations.literal: After two years he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 閩、浙盜起，命寧鎮江西。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Fujian and Zhejiang, Ning was ordered to secure Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When banditry broke out in Fujian and Zhejiang, he was ordered to pacify Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 賊至，輒擊敗之。

translations.literal: Whenever bandits came he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever rebels appeared he beat them back.

sentences.zh: 暇則詢民疾苦，境內向服。

translations.literal: In leisure he inquired into the people's hardships, and within his jurisdiction they submitted willingly.
translations.idiomatic: In quieter moments he asked after the people's hardships, and the province came to accept his rule.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，召拜禮部尚書，偕胡濙理部事。

translations.literal: At the start of Jingtai he was summoned and appointed minister of rites, administering the ministry together with Hu Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingtai reign he was made minister of rites and ran the ministry with Hu Ying.

sentences.zh: 迤北可汗遣使入貢，寧言：「宜留使數日，宴勞賜予，視也先使倍厚。

translations.literal: The khan north of the frontier sent envoys to offer tribute; Ning said: We should detain the envoys several days, feast and reward them, and treat them twice as generously as Esen's envoys.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern khan sent tribute envoys, Ning urged, "Keep them several days, feast and reward them, and treat them twice as generously as Esen's missions.

sentences.zh: 彼性多猜，二人必內構，邊患可緩。」

translations.literal: They are by nature suspicious; the two sides will surely turn against each other within, and border troubles can be eased.
translations.idiomatic: They are suspicious by nature; the two will turn on each other, and the frontier threat will ease."

sentences.zh: 帝務誠信，不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor prized sincerity and trust and would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, committed to good faith, refused.

sentences.zh: 其冬，以足疾調南刑部。

translations.literal: That winter, because of foot ailment, he was transferred to the southern Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was moved to the southern Ministry of Justice because of a foot ailment.

sentences.zh: 七年為御史莊升所劾，遣核未報。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was impeached by censor Zhuang Sheng; an investigation was dispatched but no report returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year censor Zhuang Sheng impeached him; an inquiry was sent but brought no report.

sentences.zh: 寧力詆言官，都察院再劾寧脅制言路。

translations.literal: Ning fiercely denounced the remonstrating officials; the Censorate again impeached Ning for coercing the remonstrance channel.
translations.idiomatic: Ning fiercely attacked the censors; the Censorate in turn impeached him for intimidating the remonstrance offices.

sentences.zh: 詔免其罪，錄狀示之。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned his offense and had the record shown to him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned him and had the record read to him.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，命致仕。

translations.literal: When the Yingzong Emperor was restored, he was ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yingzong Emperor was restored to the throne, he was ordered to retire.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒。

translations.literal: A year later he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 寧有才而善交權貴。

translations.literal: Ning had talent but was skilled at cultivating the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was capable but fond of cultivating the powerful.

sentences.zh: 嘗自敘前後戰功，乞世蔭。

translations.literal: He once narrated his successive battle merits himself and begged a hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: He once set out his battle record himself and asked for a hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 子堣方一歲，遂得新安衛副千戶。

translations.literal: His son Kun was only one year old, yet received the post of vice commander of a thousand in the Xin'an Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kun was only one year old yet was made vice commander of a thousand in the Xin'an Guard.

sentences.zh: 王來，字原之，慈溪人。

translations.literal: Wang Lai, style name Yuanzhi, was a man of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lai, whose style was Yuanzhi, came from Cixi.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年以會試乙榜授新建教諭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuande, on the B list of the metropolitan examination, he was appointed instructor at Xinjian.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 2 (1427) he placed on the B list of the metropolitan exam and was made instructor at Xinjian.

sentences.zh: 寧王府以諸生充樂舞，來請易以道士。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ning's household used students as ritual dancers; Lai requested that Daoist priests be used instead.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ning's household used students as ritual dancers; Lai asked that Daoist priests replace them.

sentences.zh: 諸王府設樂舞生始此。

translations.literal: The establishment of ritual-dance students in princely households began with this.
translations.idiomatic: This was the origin of ritual-dance students in princely households.

sentences.zh: 六年，以薦擢御史，出按蘇、松、常、鎮四府。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, on recommendation he was promoted to censor and sent to investigate Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, and Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was recommended and made censor, investigating Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, and Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 命偕巡撫周忱考察屬吏，敕有「請自上裁」語。

translations.literal: He was ordered together with Grand Coordinator Zhou Chen to examine subordinate officials; the edict contained the phrase "request the sovereign's decision."
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered with Grand Coordinator Zhou Chen to examine subordinate officials; the edict required them to "request the sovereign's decision."

sentences.zh: 來言：「賊民吏，去之惟恐不速，必請而後行，民困多矣。」

translations.literal: Lai said: Corrupt officials are bandits upon the people; in removing them one fears only delay—if we must request permission before acting, the people's hardship will be great.
translations.idiomatic: Lai said, "Corrupt officials prey on the people; we should remove them as fast as we can. If we must ask permission first, the people will suffer far more."

sentences.zh: 帝為改敕賜之。

translations.literal: The Emperor altered the edict for them accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor revised the edict accordingly.

sentences.zh: 中官陳武以太后命使江南，橫甚，來數抑之。

translations.literal: The eunuch Chen Wu, on the empress dowager's orders, was envoy to the south; he was extremely overbearing, and Lai repeatedly restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Chen Wu went to the south on the empress dowager's orders and behaved tyrannically; Lai repeatedly checked him.

sentences.zh: 武還，訴於帝。

translations.literal: Wu returned and complained to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wu returned and complained to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝問都御史顧佐：「巡按誰也？」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Censor-in-Chief Gu Zuo: Who is the investigating censor?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Censor-in-Chief Gu Zuo, "Who is that investigating censor?"

sentences.zh: 佐以來對。

translations.literal: Zuo answered that it was Lai.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo answered that it was Lai.

sentences.zh: 帝嘆息稱其賢，曰「識之」。

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed and praised his worth, saying, "Take note of him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and praised his worth, saying, "Remember him."

sentences.zh: 及報命，獎諭甚至。

translations.literal: When he reported on his mission, the rewards and commendations were very great.
translations.idiomatic: When he reported back, the commendation was unusually generous.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，以楊士奇薦，擢山西左參政。

translations.literal: When the Yingzong Emperor acceded, on Yang Shiji's recommendation he was promoted to left administrative vice commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yingzong Emperor came to the throne, Yang Shiji recommended him and he was made left administrative vice commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 言：「流民所在成家。

translations.literal: He said: Wandering people settle and form households wherever they are.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Wandering people settle and form households wherever they end up.

sentences.zh: 及招還故土，每以失產復逃去。

translations.literal: When summoned back to their native places, they often flee again because they have lost their property.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned home they often flee again because they have lost their land.

sentences.zh: 乞請隨在附籍便。」

translations.literal: I beg that they be allowed to register where they are.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that they be allowed to register wherever they are."

sentences.zh: 又言：「郡縣官不以農業為務，致民多遊惰，催征輒致已命。

translations.literal: He also said: County and prefectural officials do not make agriculture their business, causing many people to roam in idleness; when tax collection is pressed, lives are often lost.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Local officials neglect agriculture, so many people drift idle; when taxes are pressed, lives are lost.

sentences.zh: 朝廷憫其失業，下詔蠲除，而田日荒閑，租稅無出，累及良民。

translations.literal: The court pities their loss of livelihood and issues edicts of remission, yet fields daily lie waste, no rent is paid, and upright people are dragged down with them.
translations.idiomatic: The court pities their plight and remits taxes, yet fields lie idle, no rent is paid, and honest taxpayers are dragged down with them.

sentences.zh: 宜擇守長賢者，以課農為職。

translations.literal: Worthy prefects and magistrates should be chosen and made to take promoting agriculture as their duty.
translations.idiomatic: Choose worthy magistrates and make promoting agriculture their chief duty.

sentences.zh: 其荒田，令附近之家通力合作，供租之外，聽其均分，原主復業則還之。

translations.literal: As for waste land, let nearby households cooperate in working it; beyond paying rent, let them share the yield equally, and if the original owner returns to farming, restore it to him.
translations.idiomatic: For abandoned fields, let nearby households farm them together; after rent is paid, let them share the harvest, and return the land if the original owner resumes farming.

sentences.zh: 蠶桑可裨本業者，聽其規畫。

translations.literal: Where sericulture can supplement the basic livelihood, let them plan it.
translations.idiomatic: Where sericulture can supplement farming, let them plan it.

sentences.zh: 仍令提學風憲官督之，庶人知務本。」

translations.literal: Still order the educational and surveillance officials to supervise, so that the people may know to hold to the fundamental occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Have educational and surveillance officials oversee this so the people return to their proper work."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 來居官廉，練達政事。

translations.literal: Lai in office was incorrupt and skilled in administration.
translations.idiomatic: In office Lai was incorrupt and adept at administration.

sentences.zh: 侍郎于謙撫山西，亟稱其才，可置近侍。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Yu Qian governed Shanxi and repeatedly praised his talent, saying he could be placed in close attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Minister Yu Qian governed Shanxi he repeatedly praised Lai's talent and said he deserved a post close to the throne.

sentences.zh: 而來執法嚴，疾惡尤甚，以公事杖死縣令不職者十人。

translations.literal: But Lai enforced the law strictly and hated evil intensely; on official business he had ten negligent magistrates beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lai enforced the law harshly and hated corruption fiercely; on official business he had ten negligent magistrates beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 逮下獄，當徒。

translations.literal: He was arrested and imprisoned and sentenced to penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: He was arrested, imprisoned, and sentenced to penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 遇赦，以原官調補廣東。

translations.literal: On an amnesty he was transferred at his former rank to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty allowed him to resume his former rank in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 來自此始折節為和平，而政亦修舉。

translations.literal: From this Lai began to restrain himself and become milder, and his governance was also well conducted.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Lai moderated his manner, and his governance improved.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年遷河南左布政使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong he was transferred to left administrative commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 13 (1448) he became left administrative commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 明年改左副都御史，巡撫河南及湖廣襄陽諸府。

translations.literal: The next year he was changed to vice censor-in-chief on the left, grand coordinating Henan and the Xiangyang prefectures of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became vice censor-in-chief on the left, grand coordinating Henan and the Xiangyang prefectures of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 也先逼京師，來督兵勤王。

translations.literal: When Esen pressed the capital, Lai led troops to relieve the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen threatened the capital, Lai led troops to the emperor's relief.

sentences.zh: 渡河，聞寇退，乃引還。

translations.literal: Crossing the river, he heard the invaders had withdrawn and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the river, heard the enemy had withdrawn, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 賊平，班師。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were pacified, the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔留來、缶鎮撫。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Lai and Liang Fu to remain and pacify the region.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Lai and Liang Fu, Duke of Baoding, to remain and pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 尋命來兼巡撫貴州。

translations.literal: Soon Lai was also ordered to serve as grand coordinator of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made grand coordinator of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「近因黔、楚用兵，暫行鬻爵之例。

translations.literal: He memorialized: Recently because of military use in Qian and Chu, the temporary sale of offices was instituted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "Because of the recent campaigns in Guizhou and Huguang, the temporary sale of offices was allowed.

sentences.zh: 今寇賊稍寧，惟平越、都勻等四衛乏餉。

translations.literal: Now the bandits are somewhat quiet, but the four guards including Pingyue and Duyun lack provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Now the rebels are quieter, but the four guards including Pingyue and Duyun lack funds.

sentences.zh: 宜召商中鹽，罷納米例。」

translations.literal: Merchants should be summoned to advance salt revenue and the grain-payment scheme should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Summon merchants to advance salt revenue and abolish the grain-payment scheme."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 三年十月召還，加兼大理寺卿。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year he was summoned back and additionally made chief of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the third year he was recalled and additionally made chief of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 缶以來功大，乞加旌異。

translations.literal: Fu, because Lai's merit was great, begged special commendation for him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Fu, judging Lai's merit great, asked for special commendation.

sentences.zh: 都給事中蘇霖駁之，乃止。

translations.literal: Chief supervising secretary Su Lin rebutted it, and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Chief supervising secretary Su Lin objected, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 來還在道，以貴州苗復反，敕回師進討。

translations.literal: Lai was still on the road when Guizhou Miao rebelled again; an edict ordered him to turn back and advance in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Lai was still on the road when Guizhou Miao rebelled again; an edict ordered him to turn back and campaign.

sentences.zh: 明年，事平。

translations.literal: The next year the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the rebellion was pacified.

sentences.zh: 召為南京工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned as minister of works at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as minister of works at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，六尚書悉罷。

translations.literal: When the Yingzong Emperor was restored, all six ministers were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yingzong Emperor was restored, all six Nanjing ministers were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 來歸。

translations.literal: Lai returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Lai went home.

sentences.zh: 成化六年卒於家。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chenghua he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in Chenghua 6 (1470).

sentences.zh: 孫原貞，名瑀，以字行，德興人。

translations.literal: Sun Yuanzhen, personal name Yu, styled by his style name, was a man of Dexing.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuanzhen, personal name Yu, was known by his style; he came from Dexing.

sentences.zh: 永樂十三年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the thirteenth year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Yongle 13 (1415).

sentences.zh: 授禮部主事，歷郎中。

translations.literal: Appointed secretary in the Ministry of Rites, he rose through the ranks to director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed secretary in the Ministry of Rites and rose to director.

sentences.zh: 英宗初，用薦擢河南右參政。

translations.literal: At the start of the Yingzong reign, on recommendation he was promoted to right administrative vice commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yingzong reign he was recommended and made right administrative vice commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 居官清慎，有吏才。

translations.literal: In office he was pure and cautious and possessed administrative talent.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was scrupulous and capable as an administrator.

sentences.zh: 正統八年，大臣會薦，遷浙江左布政使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhengtong the great ministers jointly recommended him and he was transferred to left administrative commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 8 (1443) senior ministers jointly recommended him, and he became left administrative commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 久之，盜大起閩、浙間，赦而再叛。

translations.literal: After a long time banditry rose greatly between Fujian and Zhejiang; amnestied, they rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long banditry flared across Fujian and Zhejiang; pardoned once, the rebels rose again.

sentences.zh: 景帝即位，發兵討之。

translations.literal: When the Jingdi Emperor acceded, troops were sent to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingdi Emperor came to the throne, troops were sent to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 原貞嘗策賊必叛，上方略，請為備。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen had once predicted the bandits would rebel; he had drawn up plans and asked to make preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen had long predicted they would rebel again; he had drawn up plans and asked to prepare.

sentences.zh: 至是即命原貞參議軍事，深入擒其魁。

translations.literal: At this he was immediately ordered to take part in military deliberations, penetrate deep, and capture their leaders.
translations.idiomatic: He was now ordered to join the military staff, penetrate deep, and capture the rebel leaders.

sentences.zh: 而溫州余賊猶未滅，命都指揮李信為都督僉事，調軍討之。

translations.literal: But remaining bandits in Wenzhou were not yet destroyed; regional commander Li Xin was appointed vice regional commander and troops were shifted to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Remaining rebels in Wenzhou were not yet crushed; regional commander Li Xin was made vice regional commander and troops were sent against them.

sentences.zh: 遂拜原貞兵部左侍郎，參信軍務，鎮守浙江。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen was then appointed vice minister of war on the left, joined Xin's military affairs, and garrisoned Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen was then made vice minister of war on the left, joined Li Xin's staff, and garrisoned Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，當去，副都御史軒輗請留之。

translations.literal: On his mother's death he should have left office, but vice censor-in-chief Xuan Yu requested that he be kept.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he should have left office, but vice censor-in-chief Xuan Yu asked that he be retained.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The reply was approval.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年，原貞進兵搗賊巢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai, Yuanzhen advanced and struck the bandits' lair.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 1 (1450) Yuanzhen advanced and struck the rebels' lair.

sentences.zh: 俘斬賊首陶得二等，招撫三千六百余人，追還被掠男女。

translations.literal: He captured and beheaded the bandit chiefs Tao De'er and others, pacified more than 3,600 persons, and recovered abducted men and women.
translations.idiomatic: He captured and killed chiefs including Tao De'er, pacified more than 3,600 people, and recovered abducted men and women.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，璽書獎勵。

translations.literal: On report of victory an imperial letter rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Victory reported, an imperial letter praised him.

sentences.zh: 請奔喪。

translations.literal: He requested leave for mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 逾月，還鎮。

translations.literal: After a month he returned to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 復分兵剿平余寇。

translations.literal: He again divided troops and exterminated the remaining bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent detachments and wiped out the remaining rebels.

sentences.zh: 奏析瑞安地增置泰順，析麗水、青田二縣地置雲和、宣平、景寧四邑，建官置戍，盜患遂息。

translations.literal: He memorialized to carve territory from Ruian to add Taishun, and from Lishui and Qingtian to establish the four districts of Yunhe, Xuanping, and Jingning, set up officials and garrisons, and bandit trouble thus ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to carve Taishun from Ruian and the districts of Yunhe, Xuanping, and Jingning from Lishui and Qingtian, establish officials and garrisons, and banditry subsided.

sentences.zh: 論功，進秩一等。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted one grade.

sentences.zh: 浙官田賦重，右布政使楊瓚請均於民田輕額者。

translations.literal: In Zhejiang official-field land tax was heavy; Right Administrative Commissioner Yang Zan requested equalizing it with civilian fields of lighter assessment.
translations.idiomatic: Official fields in Zhejiang bore heavy land taxes; Right Administrative Commissioner Yang Zan asked that their levies be averaged with those on civilian fields assessed at lower rates.

sentences.zh: 詔原貞督之，田賦以平。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yuanzhen to supervise it, and the land tax was balanced.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Yuanzhen to oversee the reform, and land taxes were brought into balance.

sentences.zh: 三年請褒贈禦賊死事武臣。

translations.literal: In the third year he requested posthumous honors for military officers who died resisting bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he memorialized for posthumous honors for military officers who had died fighting bandits.

sentences.zh: 指揮同知脫綱、王瑛，都指揮僉事沈轔、崔源，皆得贈恤。

translations.literal: Assistant regional commanders Tuogang and Wang Ying, and vice regional commanders Shen Lin and Cui Yuan, all received posthumous gifts and pensions.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant regional commanders Tuogang and Wang Ying and vice regional commanders Shen Lin and Cui Yuan all received posthumous honors and pensions.

sentences.zh: 六月進兵部尚書，鎮守如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was promoted to Minister of War; his garrison command remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was promoted to minister of war while retaining his garrison command.

sentences.zh: 未幾，命考察福建庶官，因留鎮焉。

translations.literal: Before long he was ordered to inspect ordinary officials in Fujian and therefore remained garrisoning there.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was ordered to inspect ordinary officials in Fujian and remained on garrison duty there.

sentences.zh: 福州、建寧二府，舊有銀冶，因寇亂罷。

translations.literal: The two prefectures of Fuzhou and Jianning formerly had silver smelters, which were closed because of bandit unrest.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou and Jianning prefectures had once operated silver smelters, but these were shut down during the bandit troubles.

sentences.zh: 朝議復開，原貞執不可，乃寢。

translations.literal: The court debated reopening them; Yuanzhen firmly held it impossible, and the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated reopening the smelters; Yuanzhen firmly opposed it, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，疏言：

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year he submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifth year he submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 四方屯軍，率以營繕、轉輸諸役妨耕作。

translations.literal: Garrison armies throughout the realm are mostly blocked from farming by construction, transport, and other corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: "Garrison troops everywhere are kept from farming by construction work, transport duty, and other corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 宜簡精銳實伍，余悉歸之農。

translations.literal: We should select the elite to fill the ranks in earnest, and return all the rest to farming.
translations.idiomatic: Pick the best men to fill the ranks properly and send all the rest back to the fields.

sentences.zh: 茍增萬人屯，即歲省支倉糧十二萬石，且積余糧六萬石，兵食豈有不足哉。

translations.literal: If we added ten thousand men to farming garrisons, we would at once save one hundred twenty thousand shi of warehouse grain each year and accumulate sixty thousand shi of surplus grain—how could military provisions ever be insufficient?
translations.idiomatic: If ten thousand more men were put to garrison farming, the state would save one hundred twenty thousand shi of grain from the granaries each year and build a surplus of sixty thousand shi—would troops ever go hungry?

sentences.zh: 今歲漕數百萬石，道路費不貲。

translations.literal: This year millions of shi of grain tribute are transported; road expenses are incalculable.
translations.idiomatic: This year millions of shi of tribute grain are shipped north, and the cost of transport on the roads is beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 如浙江糧軍兌運米，石加耗米七斗。

translations.literal: For example, when Zhejiang grain soldiers deliver transport rice, seven dou of wastage grain are added per shi.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhejiang, when grain soldiers deliver transport rice, seven dou of wastage allowance is added to every shi.

sentences.zh: 民自運米，石加八斗。

translations.literal: When civilians transport their own rice, eight dou are added per shi.
translations.idiomatic: When civilians transport their own rice, eight dou are added to every shi.

sentences.zh: 其余計水程遠近加耗。

translations.literal: For the rest, wastage is added according to the distance of the water route.
translations.idiomatic: Elsewhere wastage is calculated according to the distance of the water route.

sentences.zh: 是田不加多，而賦斂實倍，欲民無困，不可得也。

translations.literal: Thus though the fields are not increased, the actual levies are doubled; to wish the people unburdened is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: The fields are no larger, yet the actual levies are doubled; to expect the people not to suffer is impossible.

sentences.zh: 況今太倉無十數年之積，脫遇水旱，其何以濟！

translations.literal: Moreover Taicang granary now has not a decade's stores; if flood or drought should come, how shall we provide relief!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Taicang now holds less than a decade's reserves; if flood or drought should strike, how would we provide relief?

sentences.zh: 宜量入為出，汰冗食浮費。

translations.literal: We should measure income and regulate expenditure, and eliminate superfluous mouths and wasteful spending.
translations.idiomatic: Income and outlay should be balanced, and useless mouths and wasteful spending cut away.

sentences.zh: 俟倉儲既裕，漸減歲漕數，而民困可蘇也。

translations.literal: Once the granaries are ample, gradually reduce the annual tribute transport, and popular distress can be relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Once the granaries are full again, the annual tribute shipments can be reduced step by step, and the people's hardship eased.

sentences.zh: 臣昔官河南，稽諸逃民籍凡二十余萬戶，悉轉徙南陽、唐、鄧、襄、樊間。

translations.literal: When I formerly served in Henan, I checked registries of escaped households—more than two hundred thousand in all—who had all moved among Nanyang, Tang, Deng, Xiang, and Fan.
translations.idiomatic: When I served in Henan I examined the registries of fugitive households: more than two hundred thousand in all, scattered among Nanyang, Tang, Deng, Xiang, and Fan.

sentences.zh: 群聚謀生，安保其不為盜？

translations.literal: Massed together seeking livelihood—how can we ensure they do not become bandits?
translations.idiomatic: Massed together and struggling to live—how can we be sure they will not turn to banditry?

sentences.zh: 宜及今年豐，遣近臣循行，督有司籍為編戶，給田業，課農桑，立社學、鄉約、義倉，使敦本務業。

translations.literal: We should take advantage of this year's abundance, send trusted ministers to tour, supervise local officials in registering them as regular households, grant fields, assign farming and mulberry duties, establish community schools, village compacts, and charity granaries, and make them devote themselves to fundamental occupations.
translations.idiomatic: We should take advantage of this year's harvest, send trusted ministers to tour the region, and have local officials register them as regular households, grant them fields, assign farming and sericulture, and establish community schools, village compacts, and charity granaries so they return to honest work.

sentences.zh: 生計既定，徐議賦役，庶無他日患。

translations.literal: Once livelihoods are settled, then slowly discuss levies and corvée—perhaps there will be no trouble hereafter.
translations.idiomatic: Once their livelihoods are secure, levies and corvée can be discussed gradually, and future trouble may be avoided."

sentences.zh: 時不能盡用。

translations.literal: At the time not all could be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court could not adopt all of it.

sentences.zh: 後劉千斤之亂，果如原貞所料。

translations.literal: Later the rebellion of Liu Qianjin indeed occurred just as Yuanzhen had foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: Later the uprising of Liu Qianjin unfolded exactly as Yuanzhen had predicted.

sentences.zh: 已，復鎮浙江。

translations.literal: Thereafter he again garrisoned Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he returned to garrison Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 英宗復位，罷歸。

translations.literal: When the Yingzong Emperor was restored to the throne, Yuanzhen was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yingzong Emperor was restored, he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 成化十年卒，年八十七。

translations.literal: He died in the tenth year of Chenghua at age eighty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chenghua 10 (1474) at the age of eighty-seven.

sentences.zh: 原貞所至有勞績，在浙江尤著名。

translations.literal: Wherever Yuanzhen served he had merit; in Zhejiang he was especially renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Yuanzhen served he left a record of achievement; his fame was greatest in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 孫需，字孚吉，成化八年進士。

translations.literal: Sun Xu, style name Fují, passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xu, style name Fují, became a jinshi in Chenghua 8 (1472).

sentences.zh: 為常州府推官，疑獄立剖，擢南京御史。

translations.literal: As reviewing official of Changzhou prefecture he instantly resolved doubtful cases and was promoted to censor at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: As reviewing official of Changzhou prefecture he cut through doubtful cases at once and was promoted to censor at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 劾僧繼曉，忤旨，予杖，出為四川副使。

translations.literal: He impeached the monk Jixiao, offended the imperial will, was given beating with rods, and sent out as vice commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached the monk Jixiao, offended the emperor, was beaten with rods, and was sent out as vice commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，累官右副都御史，巡撫河南。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi era he rose through posts to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign he rose to right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 歲兇，募民築汴河堤，堤成而饑者亦濟。

translations.literal: In a famine year he hired civilians to build the Bian River embankment; when the embankment was finished the hungry were also relieved.
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year he hired civilians to build the Bian River dike; when the work was done the hungry were fed as well.

sentences.zh: 鎮守中官劉郎貪橫。

translations.literal: The eunuch garrison commissioner Liu Lang was greedy and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch garrison commissioner Liu Lang was greedy and tyrannical.

sentences.zh: 奸民赴郎訟者，需以法論之遣戍。

translations.literal: When scoundrels went to Lang to bring lawsuits, Xu tried them by law and sent them to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: When scoundrels went to Lang to bring lawsuits, Xu tried them by law and banished them to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 郎為跪請，執不聽，郎恨次骨。

translations.literal: Lang knelt begging for mercy, but Xu would not listen; Lang hated him to the marrow.
translations.idiomatic: Lang knelt to plead for them, but Xu would not yield; Lang hated him to the bone.

sentences.zh: 大臣子橫於鄉，需抑之。

translations.literal: The son of a high minister bullied people in the countryside; Xu checked him.
translations.idiomatic: The son of a senior minister bullied people in the countryside, and Xu restrained him.

sentences.zh: 郎與謀，改需撫陜西。

translations.literal: Lang schemed with others and had Xu transferred to Grand Coordinator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Lang plotted with others and had Xu transferred to grand coordinator of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 尋改撫鄖陽，安輯流民，占籍者九萬余戶。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Grand Coordinator of Yunyang; he settled wandering people, and more than ninety thousand households were registered.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reassigned as grand coordinator of Yunyang, where he settled wandering people and registered more than ninety thousand households.

sentences.zh: 正德元年召為南京兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde he was summoned as Right Vice Minister of War at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 1 (1506) he was summoned to serve as right vice minister of war at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 四年就拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was immediately appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed minister of rites on the spot.

sentences.zh: 未兩月，劉瑾惡之，追論撫河南時事，罰米輸邊。

translations.literal: Within two months Liu Jin hated him, dredged up matters from his time as coordinator of Henan, and fined him rice sent to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Within two months Liu Jin turned against him, dredged up affairs from his tenure in Henan, and fined him grain to be sent to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 廷推需刑部尚書，中旨令致仕。

translations.literal: The court recommended Xu for Minister of Punishments; an imperial rescript ordered retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The court recommended Xu for minister of punishments, but an imperial rescript ordered him to retire.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，起南京工部尚書，就改刑部，再改吏部。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, Xu was recalled as Minister of Works at Nanjing, then immediately changed to Punishments, and again to Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed he was recalled as minister of works at Nanjing, then moved at once to punishments and afterward to personnel.

sentences.zh: 十三年乞休去。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he requested leave and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he asked to retire and left office.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初卒，謚清簡。

translations.literal: He died at the start of the Jiajing reign and was given the posthumous title Qingjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Jiajing reign and was posthumously titled Qingjian, "Pure and Simple."

sentences.zh: 張憲，字廷式，與需同里，同舉進士，相代為尚書。

translations.literal: Zhang Xian, style name Tingshi, was from the same district as Xu; both passed the jinshi examination and succeeded each other as minister.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian, style name Tingshi, came from the same home district as Xu; both became jinshi and served as minister in turn.

sentences.zh: 嘗為浙江右布政使，後以工部右侍郎督易州山廠，公帑無毫髮私。

translations.literal: He had once been Right Administrative Commissioner of Zhejiang; later, as Right Vice Minister of Works, he supervised the Yizhou mountain works and took not a hair's breadth from the public treasury for himself.
translations.idiomatic: He had served as right administrative commissioner of Zhejiang; later, as right vice minister of works, he supervised the Yizhou mountain works and never touched a coin of public funds for himself.

sentences.zh: 歷南京禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He served as Minister of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He served as minister of rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾勒致仕。

translations.literal: Liu Jin forced him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin forced him into retirement.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，起工部。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, he was recalled to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed he was recalled to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 朱鑒，字用明，晉江人。

translations.literal: Zhu Jian, style name Yongming, was a man of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jian, style name Yongming, came from Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 童時刲股療父疾。

translations.literal: As a child he cut flesh from his thigh to treat his father's illness.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he cut flesh from his thigh to treat his father's illness.

sentences.zh: 舉鄉試，授蒲圻教諭。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination and was appointed instructor at Puqi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination and was appointed instructor at Puqi.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年，與廬陵知縣孔文英等四十三人以顧佐薦，召於各道觀政三月，遂擢御史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuande, he and forty-three others including Kong Wenying, magistrate of Luling, on Gu Zuo's recommendation were summoned to observe government in the various circuits for three months, and then promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 2 (1427), he and forty-two others including Kong Wenying, magistrate of Luling, were recommended by Gu Zuo, summoned to observe government in the various circuits for three months, and then promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 巡按湖廣，諭降梅花峒賊蕭啟寧等。

translations.literal: Touring as investigating censor in Huguang, he persuaded the Meihua Cave bandits Xiao Qining and others to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: As investigating censor in Huguang he persuaded the Meihua Cave bandits, including Xiao Qining, to surrender.

sentences.zh: 請復舊制，同副使、僉事按行所部，問民疾苦。

translations.literal: He requested restoring the old system whereby the censor, together with the vice commissioner and assistant commissioner, toured the jurisdiction and inquired into the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the old practice be restored, under which the censor toured his jurisdiction together with the vice commissioner and assistant commissioner to inquire into the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 湖湘俗，男女婚嫁多逾三十。

translations.literal: In the custom of Hunan and Hubei, men and women often married only after thirty.
translations.idiomatic: In Hunan and Hubei it was customary for men and women to marry only after thirty.

sentences.zh: 鑒申明禮制，其俗遂變。

translations.literal: Jian clarified the ritual regulations, and the custom thereupon changed.
translations.idiomatic: Jian enforced the ritual code, and the custom changed.

sentences.zh: 三載代歸。

translations.literal: After three years his tour ended and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: After three years his term ended and he returned.

sentences.zh: 正統五年復按廣東。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengtong he again toured as investigating censor in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 5 (1440) he again served as investigating censor in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 奏設欽州守備都指揮。

translations.literal: He memorialized to establish a garrison regional commander at Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to establish a garrison regional commander at Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 奉命錄囚，多所平反，招撫逋叛甚眾。

translations.literal: Ordered to review prisoners, he reversed many verdicts and pacified a great many fugitive rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to review prisoners, he reversed many wrongful verdicts and pacified large numbers of fugitive rebels.

sentences.zh: 還朝，請天下按察司增僉事一人，專理屯田，遂為定制。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he requested that each provincial surveillance commission add one assistant commissioner devoted solely to garrison fields, and this became a permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he asked that every provincial surveillance commission add one assistant commissioner devoted solely to garrison fields, and this became permanent practice.

sentences.zh: 七年，用薦擢山西左參政。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, on recommendation he was promoted to Left Administrative Vice Commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was recommended and promoted to left administrative vice commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 奏減平陽采薪供邊夫役。

translations.literal: He memorialized to reduce the Pingyang corvée of gathering firewood for frontier supply.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to reduce the Pingyang corvée of gathering firewood for frontier supply.

sentences.zh: 景帝監國，進布政使。

translations.literal: When the Jingdi Emperor was regent, Jian was promoted to administrative commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingdi Emperor was regent, he was promoted to administrative commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋擢右副都御史，巡撫其地。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of that region.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of the region.

sentences.zh: 上言：「也先奸詭百端，殺掠無已。

translations.literal: He memorialized: Esen is treacherous in countless ways and kills and plunders without end.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Esen is treacherous in countless ways and kills and plunders without end.

sentences.zh: 復假和親，遣使覘伺。

translations.literal: Again feigning peace through marriage, he sends envoys to spy.
translations.idiomatic: Again feigning a marriage alliance, he sends envoys to spy.

sentences.zh: 以送駕為名，覬得開關延接。

translations.literal: Under the pretext of escorting the emperor home, he hopes to have the passes opened to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Under the pretext of escorting the captive emperor home, he hopes the passes will be opened to receive him.

sentences.zh: 稍示抗拒，彼即有辭。

translations.literal: If we show even slight resistance, he at once has a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Show even slight resistance and he at once has a pretext.

sentences.zh: 其謀既深，我慮宜遠。

translations.literal: His schemes are already deep; our forethought should be far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: His schemes run deep; our foresight must run farther.

sentences.zh: 宜暫罷中貴監軍之制，假總兵以生殺權，使誌無所撓，計有所施。

translations.literal: We should for the time suspend the system of eunuch supervision of armies, lend regional commanders the power of life and death, so that resolve is not disturbed and plans can be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: For the time being the system of eunuch army supervisors should be suspended and regional commanders granted the power of life and death, so that resolve is not undermined and plans can be executed.

sentences.zh: 整散兵，募勇士，重懸賞格。

translations.literal: Put scattered troops in order, recruit brave men, and set heavy reward scales.
translations.idiomatic: Reorganize scattered troops, recruit brave men, and offer heavy rewards.

sentences.zh: 鼓勸義旅，征勤王兵，數道並進，戮力復仇。

translations.literal: Rouse loyal volunteers, levy troops to rescue the throne, advance by several routes together, and join strength to take revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Rouse loyal volunteers, levy troops to rescue the throne, advance on several fronts at once, and join in common purpose to avenge the realm.

sentences.zh: 庶大駕可還，敵兵自退。

translations.literal: Then perhaps the imperial carriage can return and the enemy troops will withdraw of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Then perhaps the emperor can be recovered and the enemy will withdraw of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 曩者江南寇發，皆以誅王振為名。

translations.literal: Formerly when bandits rose in the Jiangnan region, they all took punishing Wang Zhen as their rallying cry.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Jiangnan before, they all rallied under the cry of punishing Wang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 夫事歸朝廷則治，歸宦官則亂。

translations.literal: When affairs rest with the court there is order; when they rest with eunuchs there is chaos.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs rest with the court there is order; when they rest with eunuchs there is chaos.

sentences.zh: 昔高皇帝與群臣議事，必屏去左右，恐泄事機。

translations.literal: Formerly the Gaozu Emperor, when deliberating with his ministers, always dismissed attendants at his side, fearing the leakage of state secrets.
translations.idiomatic: In former times the Hongwu Emperor, when deliberating with his ministers, always dismissed attendants from the room, fearing the leakage of state secrets.

sentences.zh: 乞杜權幸之門，凡軍國重事，屬任大臣，必當有濟。」

translations.literal: I beg to shut the gate to the favored and powerful; let all weighty military and state affairs be entrusted to great ministers, and there will surely be remedy.
translations.idiomatic: Shut the gate to the favored and powerful; entrust all weighty military and state affairs to senior ministers, and the realm will surely be saved."

sentences.zh: 景帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The Jingdi Emperor praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingdi Emperor praised and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 時瓦剌窺塞下，鑒日夜為守禦計。

translations.literal: At the time the Oirats watched below the passes; Jian day and night made plans for defense.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Oirats watched below the frontier passes, and Jian worked day and night on defensive plans.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年，敵數萬騎攻雁門，都指揮李端擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai, enemy forces of tens of thousands of horsemen attacked Yanmen; Regional Commander Li Duan struck and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 1 (1450) enemy forces numbering tens of thousands of horsemen attacked Yanmen; Regional Commander Li Duan drove them back.

sentences.zh: 尋犯河曲及義井堡，殺二指揮，圍忻、代諸州，石亨等不能禦。

translations.literal: Soon they invaded Hequ and Yijing Fort, killed two commanders, and besieged the prefectures of Xin and Dai; Shi Heng and others could not repel them.
translations.idiomatic: They soon raided Hequ and Yijing Fort, killed two commanders, and besieged Xin and Dai prefectures; Shi Heng and others could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 長驅抵太原城北，山西大震。

translations.literal: They drove straight to the north of Taiyuan city, and all Shanxi was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: They drove straight to the north wall of Taiyuan, and all Shanxi was shaken.

sentences.zh: 命鑒移鎮雁門，而別遣都督僉事王良鎮太原。

translations.literal: Jian was ordered to shift his garrison to Yanmen, while Vice Regional Commander Wang Liang was separately dispatched to garrison Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was ordered to shift his headquarters to Yanmen, while Vice Regional Commander Wang Liang was separately sent to garrison Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 援兵漸集，敵亦饜，乃引去。

translations.literal: Relief troops gradually gathered; the enemy also had their fill, and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Relief troops gradually gathered; the enemy, having had their fill of plunder, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時山西仍遘兵荒，鑒外飭戎備，內撫災民，勞瘁備至。

translations.literal: At the time Shanxi still suffered war and famine; Jian outwardly tightened military preparations and inwardly comforted disaster victims, exhausting himself in every way.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi was still ravaged by war and famine; Jian tightened defenses on the frontier and comforted stricken civilians within, exhausting himself in the effort.

sentences.zh: 二年十月，鎮守山西都御史羅通召還。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year, Luo Tong, Grand Coordinator garrisoning Shanxi, was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year Luo Tong, the grand coordinator garrisoning Shanxi, was recalled.

sentences.zh: 命鑒兼領其事。

translations.literal: Jian was ordered to take charge of those duties as well.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was ordered to take over those duties as well.

sentences.zh: 明年詔遣大臣行天下，黜陟有司。

translations.literal: The next year an edict dispatched great ministers to travel the realm and promote or dismiss local officials.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an edict dispatched senior ministers to tour the realm and promote or dismiss local officials.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎鄒幹至山西，多所論劾。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Zou Qian reached Shanxi and impeached many officials.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Zou Qian reached Shanxi and impeached many officials.

sentences.zh: 鑒請召幹還，幹因極論鑒徇護，帝是幹言。

translations.literal: Jian requested that Gan be recalled; Gan thereupon strongly argued that Jian showed favoritism, and the emperor sided with Gan's words.
translations.idiomatic: Jian asked that Zou be recalled; Zou thereupon argued forcefully that Jian was shielding officials, and the emperor sided with Zou.

sentences.zh: 其年十月召鑒佐院事。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year Jian was summoned to assist in Censorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That October Jian was summoned to assist in Censorate affairs.

sentences.zh: 至京，致仕去。

translations.literal: On reaching the capital he retired and departed.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital he retired.

sentences.zh: 初，景帝易儲，鑒貽大學士陳循書，言不可。

translations.literal: Initially, when the Jingdi Emperor changed the heir, Jian sent a letter to Grand Secretary Chen Xun saying it should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Jingdi Emperor changed the heir apparent, Jian wrote to Grand Secretary Chen Xun saying it should not be done.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「陛下於上皇，當避位以全大義。」

translations.literal: Moreover he said: Your Majesty, toward the Retired Emperor, ought to yield the throne to preserve the great moral principle.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Your Majesty ought to yield the throne to the Retired Emperor to uphold the greater moral obligation."

sentences.zh: 循大駭。

translations.literal: Chen Xun was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 英宗復位，鑒詣闕上表賀。

translations.literal: When the Yingzong Emperor regained the throne, Jian came to the palace gate and submitted a congratulatory memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yingzong Emperor was restored to the throne, Jian came to court and submitted a congratulatory memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「鑒老疾，何妄來？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: Jian is old and ill — why come so recklessly?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Jian is old and ailing — why did he come so rashly?

sentences.zh: 其速令還。」

translations.literal: Have him sent back at once.
translations.idiomatic: Send him back at once."

sentences.zh: 家居二十余年卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home more than twenty years and then died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for more than twenty years before he died.

sentences.zh: 楊信民，名誠，以字行，浙江新昌人。

translations.literal: Yang Xinmin, personal name Cheng, known by his style, was a native of Xinchang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xinmin, whose personal name was Cheng and who was known by his style, came from Xinchang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 鄉舉入國學。

translations.literal: Recommended from his district, he entered the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended from his district, he entered the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 宣德時，除工科給事中。

translations.literal: During the Xuande reign he was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuande reign he was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸。

translations.literal: When his mother died he returned home in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he returned home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 營葬土石必躬舁數百步，曰：「吾葬吾母而專役他人，吾不安也。」

translations.literal: When preparing the burial he always personally carried earth and stone several hundred paces, saying: I am burying my mother yet would leave all the work to others — I would not be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When preparing the burial he always personally carried earth and stone for several hundred paces, saying: "I am burying my own mother yet would leave all the labor to others — I could not rest easy."

sentences.zh: 服闋，改刑科。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was transferred to the Penal Affairs section.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he was transferred to the Penal Affairs section.

sentences.zh: 正統中，清軍江西，還奏民隱五事，多議行。

translations.literal: During the Zhengtong reign he inspected army rolls in Jiangxi; on returning he memorialized five matters of hidden popular hardship, and most were approved for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign he inspected army rolls in Jiangxi; on returning he memorialized five grievances of the people, and most were approved.

sentences.zh: 尋以王直薦，擢廣東左參議。

translations.literal: Soon, on Wang Zhi's recommendation, he was promoted to left assistant administration commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, on Wang Zhi's recommendation, he was promoted to left assistant administration commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 清操絕俗，嘗行田野，訪利弊為更置。

translations.literal: His integrity was beyond the common run; he often traveled the fields, investigated benefits and harms, and reformed what needed changing.
translations.idiomatic: His integrity was beyond the common run; he often traveled the countryside, investigated local abuses, and reformed what needed changing.

sentences.zh: 性剛負氣，按察使郭智不法，信民劾之下獄。

translations.literal: By nature he was stern and proud; Surveillance Commissioner Guo Zhi acted unlawfully, and Xinmin impeached him and had him imprisoned.
