translations.idiomatic: By nature he was stern and proud; when Surveillance Commissioner Guo Zhi broke the law, Xinmin impeached him and had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 黃翰代智，信民復發其奸。

translations.literal: Huang Han replaced Zhi, and Xinmin again exposed his wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Han replaced Guo Zhi, and Xinmin again exposed his misconduct.

sentences.zh: 已，又劾僉事韋廣，廣遂訐信民，因與翰俱被逮。

translations.literal: Later he also impeached Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Wei Guang; Guang then denounced Xinmin, and as a result both he and Han were arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also impeached Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Wei Guang; Guang then denounced Xinmin in turn, and both Huang Han and Xinmin were arrested.

sentences.zh: 軍民嘩然，詣闕下乞留信民。

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians erupted in uproar and went to the palace gate to beg that Xinmin be kept.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians erupted in uproar and went to the palace gate to beg that Xinmin be retained in office.

sentences.zh: 詔復信民官，而翰、廣鞫實，除名。

translations.literal: An edict restored Xinmin to office, while Han and Guang were tried on the facts and dismissed from service.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored Xinmin to office, while Huang Han and Wei Guang were tried on the facts and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 景帝監國，于謙薦之，命守備白羊口。

translations.literal: When the Jingdi Emperor was regent, Yu Qian recommended him and he was ordered to garrison Baiyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingdi Emperor was regent, Yu Qian recommended him and he was ordered to garrison Baiyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 會廣東賊黃蕭養圍廣州急，嶺南人乞信民，乃以為右僉都御史巡撫其地。

translations.literal: It happened that the Guangdong bandit Huang Xiaoyang was pressing the siege of Guangzhou hard; the people of Lingnan begged for Xinmin, and he was therefore made right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of that region.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Guangdong rebel Huang Xiaoyang was pressing the siege of Guangzhou hard; the people of Lingnan begged for Xinmin, and he was appointed right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of the region.

sentences.zh: 士民聞而相慶曰：「楊公來矣。」

translations.literal: Officials and commoners, hearing this, congratulated one another, saying: Master Yang has come.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners, hearing the news, congratulated one another: "Master Yang has come."

sentences.zh: 時廣州被圍久，將士戰輒敗，禁民出入，樵采絕。

translations.literal: At that time Guangzhou had long been besieged; the troops were defeated whenever they fought; the people were forbidden to enter or leave, and firewood gathering ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou had long been under siege; the garrison was defeated in every engagement; civilians were forbidden to enter or leave, and firewood gathering ceased entirely.

sentences.zh: 而鄉民避賊來者拒不納，多為賊所害，民益愁苦歸賊。

translations.literal: Yet country folk fleeing the bandits were refused admission, and many were harmed by the bandits; the people grew ever more wretched and went over to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Country folk fleeing the rebels were turned away at the gates, and many were killed by the bandits; the people grew ever more desperate and went over to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 信民至，開城門，發倉廩，刻木鍥給民，得出入。

translations.literal: When Xinmin arrived he opened the city gates, released grain from the granaries, and issued carved wooden tallies to the people so they could come and go.
translations.idiomatic: When Xinmin arrived he opened the city gates, released grain from the granaries, and issued carved wooden tallies so the people could come and go freely.

sentences.zh: 賊見木鍥曰：「此楊公所給也」，不敢傷。

translations.literal: When bandits saw the wooden tallies they said: These were issued by Master Yang, and did not dare harm the bearers.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits saw the tallies they said, "These were issued by Master Yang," and did not dare harm the bearers.

sentences.zh: 避賊者悉收保，民若更生。

translations.literal: All who fled the bandits were taken in and protected, and the people seemed to be born anew.
translations.idiomatic: All who fled the rebels were taken in and protected, and the people seemed born anew.

sentences.zh: 信民益厲甲兵，多方招撫，降者日至。

translations.literal: Xinmin further strengthened arms and armor and sought in many ways to win people over; surrendering rebels arrived daily.
translations.idiomatic: Xinmin further strengthened the garrison and sought in many ways to win people over; surrendering rebels arrived daily.

sentences.zh: 乃使使持檄入賊營，諭以恩信。

translations.literal: He then sent an envoy bearing a proclamation into the rebel camp to instruct them in grace and good faith.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent an envoy bearing a proclamation into the rebel camp to offer clemency and good faith.

sentences.zh: 蕭養曰：「得楊公一言，死不恨。」

translations.literal: Xiaoyang said: To receive one word from Master Yang — I would die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyang said: "To receive one word from Master Yang — I would die without regret."

sentences.zh: 克日請見。

translations.literal: On a set day he requested a meeting.
translations.idiomatic: On a set day he requested a meeting.

sentences.zh: 信民單車詣之，隔濠與語。

translations.literal: Xinmin went alone in a single cart to meet him and spoke with him across the moat.
translations.idiomatic: Xinmin went alone in a single cart to meet him and spoke with him across the moat.

sentences.zh: 賊黨望見，歡曰：「果楊公也！」

translations.literal: The rebel followers, seeing him from afar, rejoiced and said: It truly is Master Yang!
translations.idiomatic: The rebel followers, seeing him from afar, rejoiced: "It truly is Master Yang!"

sentences.zh: 爭羅拜，有泣下者。

translations.literal: They scrambled to bow before him, and some wept.
translations.idiomatic: They scrambled to bow before him, and some wept.

sentences.zh: 賊以大魚獻，信民受之不疑。

translations.literal: The rebels presented a large fish as a gift; Xinmin accepted it without suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels presented a large fish as a gift; Xinmin accepted it without suspicion.

sentences.zh: 張驥，字仲德，安化人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji, style Zhongde, was a native of Anhua.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji, whose style was Zhongde, came from Anhua.

sentences.zh: 永樂中舉於鄉，入國學。

translations.literal: During the Yongle reign he passed the provincial examination and entered the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign he passed the provincial examination and entered the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 宣德初授御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xuande reign he was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xuande reign he was appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 出按江西，慮囚福建，有仁廉聲。

translations.literal: He went out to inspect Jiangxi, reviewed prisoners in Fujian, and gained a reputation for benevolence and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He toured Jiangxi as investigating censor, reviewed prisoners in Fujian, and gained a reputation for benevolence and integrity.

sentences.zh: 正統八年，吏部尚書王直等應詔，博舉廷臣公廉有學行者，驥與焉。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhengtong, Minister of Personnel Wang Zhi and others, responding to an imperial edict, broadly recommended court officials who were upright, incorrupt, and learned in conduct; Ji was among them.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 8 (1443) Minister of Personnel Wang Zhi and others, responding to an imperial edict, broadly recommended upright, incorrupt, and cultivated court officials; Ji was among them.

sentences.zh: 遷大理右寺丞，巡撫山東。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and made grand coordinator of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to right assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and made grand coordinator of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 先是，濟南設撫民官，專撫流民。

translations.literal: Earlier Jinan had established officials to pacify the people, charged solely with settling displaced persons.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jinan had established officials to pacify the people, charged solely with settling displaced persons.

sentences.zh: 後反為民擾，驥奏罷之。

translations.literal: Later this instead became a burden on the people; Ji memorialized to abolish the office.
translations.idiomatic: Later the office itself became a burden on the people; Ji memorialized to abolish it.

sentences.zh: 俗遇旱，輒伐新葬冢墓，殘其肢體，以為旱所由致，名曰「打旱骨樁」，以驥言禁絕。

translations.literal: By custom, when drought struck, people would dig up newly buried graves, mutilate the corpses, and believe drought was caused thereby — a practice called beating drought bone stakes; on Ji's recommendation it was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, when drought struck people would dig up newly buried graves and mutilate the corpses, believing drought was thus caused — a practice called "beating drought bone stakes"; on Ji's recommendation it was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 還朝，進右少卿。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he was promoted to right vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to court, he was promoted to right vice minister.

sentences.zh: 已，命巡視濟寧至淮、揚饑民。

translations.literal: Later he was ordered to inspect famine victims from Jining to the Huai and Yang regions.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was ordered to inspect famine victims from Jining to the Huai and Yang regions.

sentences.zh: 驥立法捕蝗，停不急務，蠲逋發廩，民賴以濟。

translations.literal: Ji established laws for catching locusts, halted non-urgent tasks, remitted arrears and released granary grain, and the people were thereby saved.
translations.idiomatic: Ji established laws for catching locusts, halted non-urgent tasks, remitted arrears and released granary grain, and the people were thereby saved.

sentences.zh: 十三年冬，巡撫浙江。

translations.literal: In the winter of the thirteenth year he was made grand coordinator of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the thirteenth year he was made grand coordinator of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 初，慶元人葉宗留與麗水陳鑒胡聚眾盜福建寶豐諸銀礦，已而群盜自相殺，遂為亂。

translations.literal: Initially Ye Zongliu of Qingyuan and Chen Jianhu of Lishui gathered crowds to plunder the silver mines of Baofeng and elsewhere in Fujian; later the bandits turned on one another and the affair became rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Ye Zongliu of Qingyuan and Chen Jianhu of Lishui gathered bands to plunder the silver mines of Baofeng and elsewhere in Fujian; later the bandits turned on one another and the affair became open rebellion.

sentences.zh: 九年七月，福建參議竺淵往捕，被執死。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the ninth year Fujian Assistant Administration Commissioner Zhu Yuan went to capture them and was seized and killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the ninth year Fujian Assistant Administration Commissioner Zhu Yuan went to capture them and was seized and killed.

sentences.zh: 宗留僭稱王。

translations.literal: Zongliu presumptuously styled himself king.
translations.idiomatic: Zongliu presumptuously styled himself king.

sentences.zh: 時福建鄧茂七亦聚眾反，勢甚張。

translations.literal: At the time Deng Maoqi of Fujian also gathered a crowd in rebellion, and his power grew very great.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Deng Maoqi of Fujian also raised a rebellion, and his power grew very great.

sentences.zh: 宗留、鑒胡附之，流剽浙江、江西、福建境上。

translations.literal: Zongliu and Jianhu attached themselves to him and ranged in plunder across the borders of Zhejiang, Jiangxi, and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Zongliu and Jianhu joined him and ranged in plunder across the borders of Zhejiang, Jiangxi, and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 參議耿定，僉事王晟及都督僉事陳榮，指揮劉真，都指揮吳剛、龔禮，永豐知縣鄧颙，前後敗歿。

translations.literal: Assistant Administration Commissioner Geng Ding, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Wang Sheng, Vice Regional Commander Chen Rong, Commander Liu Zhen, Regional Commanders Wu Gang and Gong Li, and Yongfeng Magistrate Deng Yong were defeated and killed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Administration Commissioner Geng Ding, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Wang Sheng, Vice Regional Commander Chen Rong, Commander Liu Zhen, Regional Commanders Wu Gang and Gong Li, and Yongfeng Magistrate Deng Yong were defeated and killed one after another.

sentences.zh: 遂昌賊蘇牙、俞伯通剽蘭溪，又與相應，遠近震動。

translations.literal: The Suichang bandits Su Ya and Yu Botong plundered Lanxi and also responded in concert; near and far were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The Suichang bandits Su Ya and Yu Botong plundered Lanxi and joined the rising as well; the whole region was shaken.

sentences.zh: 驥至，遣金華知府石瑁擊斬牙等，撫定其余黨。

translations.literal: When Ji arrived he dispatched Jinhua Prefect Shi Mao to attack and behead Ya and the others, and pacified the remaining followers.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji arrived he dispatched Jinhua Prefect Shi Mao to attack and behead Su Ya and the others, and pacified the remaining followers.

sentences.zh: 而鑒胡方以爭忿殺宗留，專其眾，自稱大王，國號太平，建元泰定。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Jianhu, in a quarrel, had just killed Zongliu and taken sole command of the band; he styled himself Great King, named his state Taiping, and adopted the reign title Taiding.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Jianhu, in a quarrel, had just killed Zongliu and taken sole command of the band; he styled himself Great King, named his state Taiping, and adopted the reign title Taiding.

sentences.zh: 偽署將帥，圍處州，分掠武義、松陽、龍泉、永康、義烏、東陽、浦江諸縣。

translations.literal: He falsely appointed generals and commanders, besieged Chuzhou, and sent detachments to plunder the counties of Wuyi, Songyang, Longquan, Yongkang, Yiwu, Dongyang, and Pujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed his own generals and commanders, besieged Chuzhou, and sent detachments to plunder the counties of Wuyi, Songyang, Longquan, Yongkang, Yiwu, Dongyang, and Pujiang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，茂七死，鑒胡勢孤。

translations.literal: Before long Maoqi died and Jianhu's power stood alone and isolated.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Maoqi died and Jianhu was left isolated.

sentences.zh: 驥命麗水丞丁寧率老人王世昌等賫榜入賊巢招之，鑒胡遂偕其黨出降。

translations.literal: Ji ordered Lishui Assistant Magistrate Ding Ning to lead the elder Wang Shichang and others, bearing proclamations into the rebel nest to summon them; Jianhu then came out with his followers and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Ji ordered Lishui Assistant Magistrate Ding Ning to lead the elder Wang Shichang and others, bearing proclamations into the rebel stronghold to summon them; Jianhu then came out with his followers and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 惟陶得二不就撫，殺使者，入山為亂如故。

translations.literal: Only Tao De'er would not accept pacification; he killed the envoy and fled into the mountains to rebel as before.
translations.idiomatic: Only Tao De'er would not accept pacification; he killed the envoy and fled into the mountains to rebel as before.

sentences.zh: 時十四年四月也。

translations.literal: This was in the fourth month of the fourteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the fourth month of the fourteenth year.

sentences.zh: 驥既招降鑒胡，而別賊蘇記養等掠金華，亦為官軍所獲，賊勢乃益衰。

translations.literal: After Ji had won Jianhu's surrender, other bandits such as Su Jiyang plundered Jinhua but were also captured by government troops, and the rebel power thus declined further.
translations.idiomatic: After Ji had won Jianhu's surrender, other bandits such as Su Jiyang plundered Jinhua but were also captured by government troops, and rebel strength declined further.

sentences.zh: 其秋，景帝嗣位，召驥還，卒於道。

translations.literal: That autumn the Jingdi Emperor succeeded to the throne, recalled Ji, and Ji died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the Jingdi Emperor succeeded to the throne, recalled Ji, and Ji died on the road home.

sentences.zh: 驥所至，鹹有建樹，山東、兩浙民久而思之。

translations.literal: Wherever Ji went he achieved results; the people of Shandong and the two Zhes long remembered him.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Ji went he achieved results; the people of Shandong and the two Zhes long remembered him.

sentences.zh: 鑒胡至京，帝宥不誅。

translations.literal: Jianhu reached the capital; the Emperor pardoned him and did not execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Jianhu reached the capital; the Emperor pardoned him and did not execute him.

sentences.zh: 更遇赦，釋充留守衛軍。

translations.literal: He later met with an amnesty and was released to serve as garrison troops at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He later benefited from an amnesty and was released to serve as a garrison soldier at the capital.

sentences.zh: 也先入犯，鑒胡乘間亡，被獲，伏誅。

translations.literal: When Esen invaded, Jianhu seized an opening and fled; he was captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen invaded, Jianhu seized an opening and fled; he was captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 竺淵，奉化人。

translations.literal: Zhu Yuan was a native of Fenghua.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yuan was a native of Fenghua.

sentences.zh: 耿定，和州人。

translations.literal: Geng Ding was a native of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Ding was a native of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 王晟鄆城人。

translations.literal: Wang Sheng was a native of Yuncheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sheng was a native of Yuncheng.

sentences.zh: 鄧颙，樂昌人。

translations.literal: Deng Yong was a native of Lechang.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yong was a native of Lechang.

sentences.zh: 俱進士。

translations.literal: All were jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: All were jinshi.

sentences.zh: 颙兵潰被執，不屈死。

translations.literal: Yong's troops were routed; he was captured and died refusing to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's troops were routed; he was captured and died refusing to submit.

sentences.zh: 詔為營葬。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that burial be arranged for him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that burial be arranged for him.

sentences.zh: 淵等贈官，錄一子。

translations.literal: Yuan and the others were posthumously granted office, and one son of each was enrolled in service.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and the others were posthumously granted office, and one son of each was enrolled in service.

sentences.zh: 馬謹，字守禮，新樂人。

translations.literal: Ma Jin, style Shouli, was a native of Xinle.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jin, whose style was Shouli, came from Xinle.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the second year of Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Xuande 2 (1427).

sentences.zh: 事父母孝，遭喪，親負土以葬。

translations.literal: He served his parents filially; when they died he personally carried earth for their burial.
translations.idiomatic: He served his parents filially; when they died he personally carried earth for their burial.

sentences.zh: 正統中，以御史按浙江。

translations.literal: During the Zhengtong reign he served as censor inspecting Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign he served as investigating censor in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 時修備倭海船，征材於嚴、衢諸郡。

translations.literal: At the time warships against Japanese pirates were being repaired and materials were levied from the prefectures of Yan and Qu.
translations.idiomatic: At the time warships against Japanese pirates were being repaired and materials were levied from the prefectures of Yan and Qu.

sentences.zh: 謹恐軍士藉勢肆斬伐，請禁飭之，報可。

translations.literal: Jin feared soldiers would rely on their power to cut timber recklessly; he requested that this be forbidden and disciplined, and the reply approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin feared soldiers would abuse their authority to cut timber recklessly; he requested that this be forbidden and disciplined, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 所至，貪猾屏跡。

translations.literal: Wherever he went, the greedy and cunning vanished from sight.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went, the greedy and cunning vanished from sight.

sentences.zh: 疏振臺、處、寧、紹四府饑。

translations.literal: He memorialized relief for famine in the four prefectures of Tai, Chu, Ning, and Shao.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized relief for famine in the four prefectures of Tai, Chu, Ning, and Shao.

sentences.zh: 吏部驗封郎中缺人久，帝令推擇。

translations.literal: The post of director in the Ministry of Personnel's Credentials Verification Bureau had long gone unfilled; the Emperor ordered candidates to be selected.
translations.idiomatic: The post of director in the Ministry of Personnel's Credentials Verification Bureau had long gone unfilled; the Emperor ordered candidates to be selected.

sentences.zh: 會謹九載滿，尚書郭琎薦謹廉直，遂用之。

translations.literal: It happened that Jin's nine-year term was complete; Minister Guo Jin recommended Jin as upright and incorrupt, and he was therefore appointed.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin's nine-year term was complete, Minister Guo Jin recommended him as upright and incorrupt, and he was appointed.

sentences.zh: 十年薦擢湖廣右布政使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was recommended and promoted to right administrative commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was recommended and promoted to right administrative commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 正統末，湖南叛苗掠靖州。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhengtong reign rebellious Miao in Hunan plundered Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhengtong reign rebellious Miao in Hunan plundered Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 命謹同御史侯爵撫諭，參將張善率兵繼之。

translations.literal: Jin was ordered, together with Censor Hou Jue, to pacify and instruct them; Assistant Regional Commander Zhang Shan led troops to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was ordered, together with Censor Hou Jue, to pacify and instruct them; Assistant Regional Commander Zhang Shan led troops in support.

sentences.zh: 謹等至，招數千人復業，其出掠者擊敗之。

translations.literal: When Jin and the others arrived they summoned several thousand people back to their livelihoods and defeated those who went out raiding.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin and the others arrived they brought several thousand people back to their livelihoods and defeated those who went out raiding.

sentences.zh: 尋與善破淇溪諸寨。

translations.literal: Soon, together with Shan, he broke the stockades of Qixi and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, together with Shan, he broke the stockades of Qixi and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，復與善大破臘婆諸洞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingtai he again joined Shan in a great defeat of the caves of Laba and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingtai he again joined Shan in a great defeat of the caves of Laba and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 已，同參將李震擊破青龍渡、馬楊山諸賊，追奔至雞心嶺，先後斬首千四百有奇。

translations.literal: Later, together with Assistant Regional Commander Li Zhen, he broke the bandits at Qinglong Ford, Mayang Mountain, and elsewhere, pursued the fleeing enemy to Jixin Ridge, and in all beheaded more than fourteen hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Later, together with Assistant Regional Commander Li Zhen, he broke the bandits at Qinglong Ford, Mayang Mountain, and elsewhere, pursued the fleeing enemy to Jixin Ridge, and in all beheaded more than fourteen hundred.

sentences.zh: 師還，靖州賊復出掠，搗其巢，斬獲如前。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the Jingzhou bandits again came out to plunder; their nests were struck and heads and captives taken as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, the Jingzhou bandits again came out to plunder; their nests were struck and heads and captives taken as before.

sentences.zh: 武岡、城溪諸賊結廣西蠻，據青肺山，復與震攻破之。

translations.literal: The bandits of Wugang, Chengxi, and elsewhere joined with Guangxi tribesmen, held Qingfei Mountain, and were again broken by Jin together with Li Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits of Wugang, Chengxi, and elsewhere joined with Guangxi tribesmen, held Qingfei Mountain, and were again broken by Jin together with Li Zhen.

sentences.zh: 獲賊楊光拳等五百六十人，斬首倍之。

translations.literal: They captured five hundred sixty bandits including Yang Guangquan and beheaded twice that number.
translations.idiomatic: They captured five hundred sixty bandits including Yang Guangquan and beheaded twice that number.

sentences.zh: 扶城諸寨，聞風款附。

translations.literal: The stockades of Fucheng and elsewhere, hearing the news, came over in submission.
translations.idiomatic: The stockades of Fucheng and elsewhere, hearing the news, came over in submission.

sentences.zh: 謹出入行間三歲，沖冒鋒鏑，與諸將同，而運籌轉餉功尤多。

translations.literal: Jin went in and out among the ranks for three years, braving arrows and blades together with the generals, yet his achievements in planning and moving supplies were especially great.
translations.idiomatic: Jin went in and out among the ranks for three years, braving arrows and blades together with the generals, yet his achievements in planning and moving supplies were especially great.

sentences.zh: 轉左布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to left administrative commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to left administrative commissioner.

sentences.zh: 錄功，進秩一等。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded, and his rank was advanced one grade.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his merit, his rank was raised one grade.

sentences.zh: 六年五月，遷右副都御史，仍支二品俸。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixth year, he was transferred to right vice censor-in-chief, still drawing salary of the second rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the sixth year he was made right vice censor-in-chief, while continuing to receive a second-rank salary.

sentences.zh: 巡撫河南，撫流民三萬一千余戶。

translations.literal: As grand coordinator of Henan, he settled more than thirty-one thousand refugee households.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as grand coordinator of Henan, he resettled more than thirty-one thousand refugee households.

sentences.zh: 天順初，廢巡撫官，謹亦罷歸，久之卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun, the grand coordinator posts were abolished; Jin also was dismissed and returned home, and after a long time died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshun reign the grand coordinator posts were abolished; Jin was dismissed and sent home, and died some time later.

sentences.zh: 謹性廉介，楊士奇嘗稱為「冰霜鐵石」。

translations.literal: Jin by nature was incorruptible and upright; Yang Shiqi once praised him as "frost, ice, iron, and stone."
translations.idiomatic: Jin was by nature incorruptible and upright; Yang Shiqi once called him "frost, ice, iron, and stone."

sentences.zh: 程信，字彥實，其先休寧人。

translations.literal: Cheng Xin, style name Yanshi, his ancestors were men of Xiuning.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xin, style name Yanshi, came from a family originally of Xiuning.

sentences.zh: 洪武中戍河間，因家焉。

translations.literal: During Hongwu he was garrisoned at Hejian, and his family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu reign he was posted to garrison duty at Hejian, and his family made its home there.

sentences.zh: 信舉正統七年進士，授吏科給事中。

translations.literal: Xin passed the jinshi examination in the seventh year of Zhengtong and was appointed a supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel section.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xin passed the jinshi examination in Zhengtong 7 and was appointed a supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel section of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 景帝即位，薦起薛瑄等三人。

translations.literal: When the Jing Emperor took the throne, he recommended and recalled Xue Xuan and two others.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing took the throne, he recommended that Xue Xuan and two others be recalled to office.

sentences.zh: 也先犯京師，信督軍守西城，上言五事。

translations.literal: Esen attacked the capital; Xin supervised troops defending the western wall and memorialized with five recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen attacked the capital, Cheng Xin directed troops defending the western wall and submitted five recommendations to the throne.

sentences.zh: 都督孫鏜擊也先失利，欲入城，信不納，督軍從城上發箭炮助之。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Sun Tang, attacking Esen, met defeat and wished to enter the city; Xin would not admit him, but directed troops from atop the wall to launch arrows and cannon to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Sun Tang had been beaten in his attack on Esen and tried to re-enter the city; Cheng Xin refused him entry but directed troops on the wall to rain arrows and cannon fire in support.

sentences.zh: 鏜戰益力，也先遂卻。

translations.literal: Tang fought with redoubled effort, and Esen thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tang redoubled his fighting, and Esen eventually withdrew.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年請振畿輔饑民，復河間學官、生徒因用兵罷遣者，皆報可。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai he requested relief for famine victims in the metropolitan districts, restoration of Hejian educational officials and students dismissed because of military affairs—all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 1 he requested famine relief for the metropolitan districts and the restoration of Hejian's school officials and students who had been dismissed for war service; all was approved.

sentences.zh: 進左給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to left supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 以天變上中興固本十事。

translations.literal: On account of heaven-sent calamities he submitted ten proposals for reviving the dynasty and securing its foundations.
translations.idiomatic: Citing heaven-sent omens, he submitted ten proposals for reviving the dynasty and strengthening its foundations.

sentences.zh: 其言敬天，則請帝敦孝友之實以答天心。

translations.literal: In speaking of revering Heaven, he asked the Emperor to fulfill the substance of filial piety and brotherliness to answer Heaven's mind.
translations.idiomatic: On revering Heaven, he urged the Emperor to embody true filial piety and fraternity in order to answer Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and adopted them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised and accepted his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 明年二月出為山東右參政，督餉遼東。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year he went out as right vice administrator of Shandong, supervising grain supplies for Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year he was posted as right vice administrator of Shandong to supervise grain supplies for Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 巡撫寇深奏盜糧一石以上者死，又置新斛視舊加大，屬信鉤考。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Kou Shen memorialized that grain thieves of one shi or more should die, and also had new measuring huo made larger than the old ones, assigning Xin to investigate and verify.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Kou Shen proposed the death penalty for anyone who stole a shi of grain or more, and had new grain measures made larger than the old standard; Cheng Xin was ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 信立碎之，曰：「奈何納人於死！」

translations.literal: Xin immediately smashed them, saying: "How can one consign people to death!"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xin immediately smashed them, saying, "How can you send people to their deaths!"

sentences.zh: 深由是不悅信。

translations.literal: From this Shen came to dislike Xin.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Kou Shen bore a grudge against Cheng Xin.

sentences.zh: 尋以憂去，服闋，起四川參政。

translations.literal: Before long he left office on account of mourning; when the mourning period ended, he was recalled as vice administrator of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon left office to mourn; when his mourning ended he was recalled as vice administrator of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 理松潘餉，偕侍郎羅綺破黑虎諸寨。

translations.literal: He managed supplies for Songpan, and together with Vice Minister Luo Qi broke the stockades of Heihu and others.
translations.idiomatic: He managed grain supplies for Songpan and, together with Vice Minister Luo Qi, captured the Heihu stockades and others.

sentences.zh: 明年，改左僉都御史，巡撫遼東。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to left assistant censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became left assistant censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 都指揮夏霖恣不法，僉事胡鼎發其四十罪，信以聞，下霖錦衣獄。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Xia Lin behaved lawlessly at will; Commissioner Hu Ding exposed forty of his crimes; Xin reported it, and Lin was put in the Embroidered-Uniform Prison.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Xia Lin ran riot with impunity; Commissioner Hu Ding laid bare forty crimes he had committed; Cheng Xin reported the matter, and Xia Lin was sent to the Embroidered-Uniform Prison.

sentences.zh: 門達言信不當代奏，帝責令陳狀。

translations.literal: Men Da said Xin ought not to have submitted on another's behalf; the Emperor rebuked him and ordered him to explain himself in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Men Da argued that Cheng Xin should not have submitted the memorial on another's behalf; the Emperor rebuked him and ordered him to explain his conduct.

sentences.zh: 時寇深方掌都察院，修前郤，劾信。

translations.literal: At the time Kou Shen was in charge of the Censorate, nursed an old grudge, and impeached Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Shen was then head of the Censorate; he settled an old score and impeached Cheng Xin.

sentences.zh: 征下詔獄，降南京太仆少卿。

translations.literal: Summoned and cast into the imperial prison, he was demoted to vice minister of the Nanjing Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned, imprisoned in the imperial prison, and demoted to vice minister of the Nanjing Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 五年召為刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was recalled as right vice minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was recalled as right vice minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 成化元年起兵部，尋轉左。

translations.literal: In Chenghua 1 he was appointed to the Ministry of War, and soon transferred to the left.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 1 he was appointed to the Ministry of War, and soon became left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 四川戎縣山都掌蠻數叛，陷合江等九縣。

translations.literal: The Shanduzhang Miao of Rong County, Sichuan, repeatedly rebelled and overran Hejiang and eight other counties.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanduzhang Miao of Rong County in Sichuan rose repeatedly, overrunning Hejiang and eight other counties.

sentences.zh: 廷議發大軍討之。

translations.literal: The court discussed dispatching a great army to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated sending a large army to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 以襄城伯李瑾充總兵官，太監劉恒為監督，進信尚書，提督軍務。

translations.literal: Li Jin, Baron of Xiangcheng, was appointed supreme commander; the eunuch Liu Heng served as supervisor; Xin was promoted to minister and put in charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jin, Baron of Xiangcheng, was made supreme commander; the eunuch Liu Heng served as supervisor; Cheng Xin was promoted to minister and placed in overall command of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 至永寧，分道進。

translations.literal: Reaching Yongning, they advanced by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Yongning, they advanced along separate routes.

sentences.zh: 都督芮成由戎縣；

translations.literal: Regional Commander Rui Cheng by way of Rong County;
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Rui Cheng by way of Rong County;

sentences.zh: 巡撫貴州都御史陳宜、參將吳經由芒部；

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-Chief of Guizhou Chen Yi and regional vice commander Wu Jing by way of Mangbu;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-Chief of Guizhou Chen Yi and regional vice commander Wu Jing by way of Mangbu;

sentences.zh: 都指揮崔旻由普市冰腦；

translations.literal: Regional Commander Cui Min by way of Pushi Bingnao;
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Cui Min by way of Pushi Bingnao;

sentences.zh: 南寧伯毛榮由李子關；

translations.literal: Mao Rong, Baron of Nanning, by way of Lizi Pass;
translations.idiomatic: Mao Rong, Baron of Nanning, by way of Lizi Pass;

sentences.zh: 巡撫四川都御史汪浩、參將宰用由渡船鋪；

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-Chief of Sichuan Wang Hao and regional vice commander Zai Yong by way of Duchuanpu;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-Chief of Sichuan Wang Hao and regional vice commander Zai Yong by way of Duchuanpu;

sentences.zh: 左右遊擊將軍羅秉忠、穆義由金鵝池；

translations.literal: The left and right mobile-detachment generals Luo Bingzhong and Mu Yi by way of Jine Chi;
translations.idiomatic: The left and right mobile-detachment generals Luo Bingzhong and Mu Yi by way of Jine Chi;

sentences.zh: 而信與瑾居中節制。

translations.literal: While Xin and Jin held the center and directed operations.
translations.idiomatic: While Cheng Xin and Li Jin held the center and directed operations.

sentences.zh: 轉戰六日，破龍背、豹尾諸寨七百五十余。

translations.literal: After six days of successive battles they broke more than seven hundred fifty stockades including Longbei and Baowei.
translations.idiomatic: After six days of continuous fighting they took more than seven hundred fifty stockades, including Longbei and Baowei.

sentences.zh: 明年至大壩，焚寨千四百五十。

translations.literal: The next year they reached Daba and burned one thousand four hundred fifty stockades.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they reached Daba and burned one thousand four hundred fifty stockades.

sentences.zh: 前後斬首四千五百有奇，俘獲無算。

translations.literal: In all they beheaded more than four thousand five hundred, and captives and booty were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In all they took more than four thousand five hundred heads, while captives and booty were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 按諸九姓不奉化者遷瀘州衛，於渡船鋪增置關堡。

translations.literal: According to investigation, the unsubmissive among the nine surname groups were relocated to Luzhou Guard, and frontier passes and forts were added at Duchuanpu.
translations.idiomatic: Those among the nine surname groups who would not submit were relocated to Luzhou Guard, and new passes and forts were established at Duchuanpu.

sentences.zh: 改大壩為太平川長官司，分山都掌地，設官建治控制之。

translations.literal: Daba was changed to the chief's office of Taipingchuan; Shanduzhang territory was divided, officials were established, and governance was set up to control it.
translations.idiomatic: Daba was reorganized as the Taipingchuan native chieftaincy; Shanduzhang lands were partitioned, officials appointed, and permanent administration established to keep control.

sentences.zh: 帝降璽書嘉勞。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent down an imperial letter with a seal to praise and reward them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor issued an imperial commendation bearing the imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 錄功，進兼大理寺卿，與白圭同蒞兵部。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded; he was promoted and also made chief minister of the Court of Judicial Review, and together with Bai Gui jointly directed the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his merit he was promoted and concurrently appointed chief minister of the Court of Judicial Review; he and Bai Gui jointly directed the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 言官劾信上首功不實。

translations.literal: Censorial officials impeached Xin for exaggerating the number of heads in his report.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials impeached Cheng Xin for inflating the head count in his victory report.

sentences.zh: 信四疏乞休，不許。

translations.literal: Xin submitted four memorials begging retirement; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xin four times asked to retire; each time the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 信欲有為，而阻於圭，不自得，數稱疾。

translations.literal: Xin wished to act, but was blocked by Gui and felt ill at ease, and repeatedly pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xin wished to accomplish things, but Bai Gui stood in his way; frustrated, he repeatedly claimed illness.

sentences.zh: 六年春旱，應詔言兵事宜更張者四，兵弊宜申理者五。

translations.literal: In the spring drought of the sixth year, in response to an imperial edict he spoke of four matters in military affairs that should be reformed and five abuses that should be clarified.
translations.idiomatic: During the spring drought of the sixth year, answering an imperial edict, he set forth four military reforms that were needed and five abuses that ought to be cleared up.

sentences.zh: 大略言：延綏、兩廣歲遭劫掠，宜擇大臣總制；

translations.literal: In general he said: Yan-Sui and the two Guang provinces suffer raiding every year—great ministers should be chosen to take overall command;
translations.idiomatic: In general he argued that Yan-Sui and the two Guang provinces suffered raids every year, and that senior ministers ought to be chosen to take overall command;

sentences.zh: 四方流民多聚荊、襄，宜早區畫；

translations.literal: Refugees from all directions gather heavily in Jing and Xiang—measures ought early to be planned;
translations.idiomatic: refugees from all quarters had gathered heavily in Jing and Xiang, and ought early to be organized and settled;

sentences.zh: 京軍操練無法，功次升賞未當。

translations.literal: Metropolitan troops are drilled without proper method, and promotions and rewards by merit roll are improper.
translations.idiomatic: metropolitan troops were drilled without proper method, and promotions and rewards by merit roll were improper.

sentences.zh: 語多侵圭。

translations.literal: His language often encroached on Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Much of what he said cut at Bai Gui.

sentences.zh: 圭奏寢之。

translations.literal: Gui memorialized and had it shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Gui memorialized the throne and had the proposals shelved.

sentences.zh: 改南京兵部，參贊機務。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of War to assist in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of War to assist in deliberations on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年致仕，逾年卒。

translations.literal: The next year he retired; after a year he died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he retired from office; he died a year later.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚襄毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with posthumous name Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 信有才力，識大體。

translations.literal: Xin had talent and capacity, and understood the larger pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xin was capable and understood the larger principles of governance.

sentences.zh: 征南蠻時，制許便宜從事。

translations.literal: When campaigning against the southern tribes, the regulations allowed him to act at discretion as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign he was authorized to act at discretion as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 迄班師，未嘗擅賞、戮一人。

translations.literal: Until the army returned, he never on his own authority rewarded or executed a single person.
translations.idiomatic: Until the army returned he never on his own authority rewarded or executed anyone.

sentences.zh: 曰：「刑賞，人主大柄也，不得已而假之人。

translations.literal: He said: "Punishment and reward are the great prerogatives of the ruler; only when unavoidable are they delegated to others.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Punishment and reward are the great prerogatives of the ruler; only when unavoidable are they delegated to others.

sentences.zh: 幸而事集，輒自專，非人臣所宜。」

translations.literal: If matters fortunately succeed and one then acts on one's own authority, that is not what a minister should do."
translations.idiomatic: If matters fortunately succeed and one then acts on one's own authority, that is not what a minister should do."

sentences.zh: 在南京，守備臣欲預錢谷訟獄事，信曰：「守備重臣，所以謹非常也。

translations.literal: In Nanjing, the defense commandant wished to intervene in matters of revenue, grain, lawsuits, and punishments; Xin said: "The defense commandant is a weighty official, whose purpose is to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: In Nanjing the defense commandant wished to intervene in revenue, grain, lawsuits, and punishments; Cheng Xin said, "The defense commandant is a weighty official whose purpose is to guard against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 若此，乃有司職耳。」

translations.literal: Affairs such as these are simply the duties of regular officials."
translations.idiomatic: Affairs such as these are simply the duties of regular officials."

sentences.zh: 論者韙之。

translations.literal: Commentators approved his view.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators praised his stand.

sentences.zh: 子敏政，見《文苑傳》。

translations.literal: His son Minzheng is treated in the "Treatise on Men of Letters."
translations.idiomatic: His son Minzheng is biographied in the Treatise on Men of Letters.

sentences.zh: 白圭，字宗玉，南宮人。

translations.literal: Bai Gui, style name Zongyu, was a man of Nangong.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Gui, style name Zongyu, was a native of Nangong.

sentences.zh: 正統七年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the seventh year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengtong 7.

sentences.zh: 除御史，監朱勇軍，討兀良哈有功。

translations.literal: Appointed censor, he oversaw Zhu Yong's army in campaigning against Wuliangha and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed censor, he oversaw Zhu Yong's army in the campaign against Wuliangha and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 巡按山西，辨疑獄百余。

translations.literal: Touring and inspecting Shanxi, he resolved more than a hundred doubtful cases.
translations.idiomatic: On an inspection tour of Shanxi he cleared more than a hundred doubtful cases.

sentences.zh: 從車駕北征，陷土木。

translations.literal: He accompanied the imperial carriage on the northern campaign and was trapped at Tumu.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on the northern expedition and was caught in the disaster at Tumu.

sentences.zh: 脫還，景帝命往澤州募兵。

translations.literal: After escaping and returning, the Jing Emperor ordered him to go to Zezhou to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: After he escaped and returned, Emperor Jing ordered him to Zezhou to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 尋遷陜西按察副使，擢浙江右布政使。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to vice commissioner of the Shaanxi surveillance commission, then promoted to right administrative commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice commissioner of the Shaanxi surveillance commission, then promoted to right administrative commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 福建賊鄭懷冒流剽處州，協諸將平之。

translations.literal: The Fujian bandit Zheng Huai, posing as a refugee, plundered at Chuzhou; he coordinated the generals and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: The Fujian bandit Zheng Huai, posing as a refugee, raided Chuzhou; Bai Gui coordinated the generals and suppressed him.

sentences.zh: 天順二年，貴州東苗幹把豬等僭號，攻劫都勻諸處。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianshun, Gan Baizhu and others of the Eastern Miao in Guizhou arrogated titles and attacked and plundered the districts around Duyun.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 2, Gan Baizhu and others of the Eastern Miao in Guizhou declared themselves kings and raided the Duyun region.

sentences.zh: 詔進右副都御史，贊南和侯方瑛軍往討。

translations.literal: An edict promoted him to right vice censor-in-chief to assist Fang Ying, Marquis of Nanhe, in leading an army to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted him to right vice censor-in-chief to assist Fang Ying, Marquis of Nanhe, in leading troops against them.

sentences.zh: 圭以谷種諸夷為東苗羽翼，先剿破百四十七寨。

translations.literal: Gui took the tribes of Guzhong and others as the wings of the Eastern Miao and first destroyed one hundred forty-seven stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Gui regarded the Guzhong tribes and others as allies of the Eastern Miao and first destroyed one hundred forty-seven stockades.

sentences.zh: 遂會兵青崖，復破四百七十余寨，乘勝攻六美山。

translations.literal: Thereupon he united forces at Qingya, again broke more than four hundred seventy stockades, and pressed the advantage to attack Mount Liumei.
translations.idiomatic: He then united his forces at Qingya, took another four hundred seventy-odd stockades, and pressed the attack on Mount Liumei.

sentences.zh: 幹把豬就擒，諸苗震詟。

translations.literal: Gan Baizhu was captured; the various Miao were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Baizhu was captured, and the Miao bands were stricken with fear.

sentences.zh: 湖廣災，就命圭巡撫。

translations.literal: When Huguang suffered disasters, Gui was immediately appointed grand coordinator there.
translations.idiomatic: When Huguang was stricken by disaster, he was appointed on the spot as grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 四年召為兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was recalled as right vice minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was recalled as right vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 明年，孛來寇莊浪。

translations.literal: The next year, Bo Lai raided Zhuanglang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Bo Lai raided Zhuanglang.

sentences.zh: 圭與都御史王竑贊都督馮宗軍務，分兵巡邊。

translations.literal: Gui together with Censor-in-Chief Wang Hong assisted Regional Commander Feng Zong in military affairs, dividing troops to patrol the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Gui and Censor-in-Chief Wang Hong assisted Regional Commander Feng Zong in military affairs, dividing forces to patrol the frontier.

sentences.zh: 圭敗之固原州。

translations.literal: Gui defeated him at Guyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Gui defeated him at Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 七年進工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 成化元年，荊、襄賊劉千斤等作亂。

translations.literal: In Chenghua 1, the bandits Liu Qianjin and others of Jing and Xiang rose in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 1, Liu Qianjin and other rebels rose in Jing and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 敕撫寧伯朱永為總兵官，都督喜信、鮑政為左右參將，中官唐慎、林貴奉監之，而以圭提督軍務，發京軍及諸道兵會討。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Zhu Yong, Baron of Funing, as supreme commander; Regional Commanders Xi Xin and Bao Zheng as left and right vice commanders; the eunuchs Tang Shen and Lin Gui to serve as supervisors; and Gui to direct military affairs, dispatching metropolitan troops and forces from various circuits to join in the suppression.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Zhu Yong, Baron of Funing, supreme commander; Xi Xin and Bao Zheng regional commanders as his lieutenants; eunuchs Tang Shen and Lin Gui supervisors; and Bai Gui overall director of military affairs, with metropolitan troops and regional forces converging for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 千斤，名通，河南西華人。

translations.literal: Qianjin, personal name Tong, was a man of Xihua in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Qianjin—personal name Tong—was from Xihua in Henan.

sentences.zh: 縣門石狻猊重千斤，通只手舉之，因以為號。

translations.literal: The stone suanni lion at the county gate weighed a thousand jin; Tong lifted it with one hand, and thus took it as his nickname.
translations.idiomatic: A stone suanni lion at the county gate weighed a thousand jin; Tong lifted it one-handed and took that as his nickname.

sentences.zh: 正統中，流民聚荊、襄間，通竄入為妖言，潛謀倡亂。

translations.literal: During Zhengtong, refugees gathered between Jing and Xiang; Tong slipped in among them spreading heterodox talk and secretly plotted to incite rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign refugees gathered in Jing and Xiang; Tong hid among them spreading seditious talk and secretly plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 石龍者，號石和尚，聚眾剽掠。

translations.literal: One called Shi Long, nicknamed the Stone Monk, gathered a crowd and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: A man called Shi Long, known as the Stone Monk, gathered followers and raided the countryside.

sentences.zh: 通與共起兵，偽稱漢王，建元德勝，流民從者四萬人。

translations.literal: Tong joined him in raising troops, falsely styled himself King of Han, established the era name Desheng, and forty thousand refugees followed.
translations.idiomatic: Tong joined him in revolt, proclaimed himself King of Han, adopted the era name Desheng, and drew forty thousand refugees to his banner.

sentences.zh: 圭等至南漳，賊迎戰，敗之，乘勝逼其巢。

translations.literal: When Gui and the others reached Nanzhang, the rebels came out to fight; they were defeated, and pressing the advantage they closed on their lair.
translations.idiomatic: When Bai Gui's force reached Nanzhang the rebels came out to fight; he defeated them and pressed on toward their stronghold.

sentences.zh: 通奔壽陽，謀走陜西。

translations.literal: Tong fled to Shouyang and planned to escape into Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tong fled to Shouyang and planned to escape west into Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 圭遣兵扼其道，通乃退保大市，與苗龍合。

translations.literal: Gui sent troops to block his path; Tong thereupon withdrew to hold Dashi and joined with Miao Long.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Gui sent troops to cut off his route; Tong withdrew to Dashi and joined forces with Miao Long.

sentences.zh: 官軍又破之雁坪，斬通子聰及其黨苗虎等。

translations.literal: The government troops again defeated them at Yanping, beheading Tong's son Cong and his follower Miao Hu and others.
translations.idiomatic: The government troops defeated them again at Yanping, beheading Tong's son Cong along with Miao Hu and other partisans.

sentences.zh: 賊退保後巖山，據險下木石如雨。

translations.literal: The rebels withdrew to hold Houyan Mountain, seized the defiles, and rained down timber and stones like rain.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fell back to Houyan Mountain, held the heights, and hurled timber and stones down like a storm.

sentences.zh: 諸軍四面攻，圭往來督戰，士皆蟻附登。

translations.literal: The armies attacked from all four sides; Gui went back and forth supervising the battle, and the soldiers all climbed up like ants clinging.
translations.idiomatic: The armies assaulted from every side. Bai Gui rode the lines urging them on, and his men swarmed up the slopes like ants.

sentences.zh: 賊大敗。

translations.literal: The rebels were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were routed.

sentences.zh: 擒通及其眾三千五百余人，獲賊子女萬一千有奇，焚其廬舍，夷險阻而還。

translations.literal: They captured Tong and more than three thousand five hundred of his followers, seized over eleven thousand of the rebels' women and children, burned their dwellings, leveled the dangerous passes, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They took Tong and more than thirty-five hundred of his men, captured over eleven thousand women and children, burned the rebel camps, cleared the mountain strongholds, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 石龍與其黨劉長子等逸去，轉掠四川，連陷巫山、大昌。

translations.literal: Shi Long and his partisan Liu Changzi and others escaped, turned to plunder Sichuan, and in succession captured Wushan and Dachang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Long and his lieutenant Liu Changzi got away, swung into Sichuan, and took Wushan and Dachang in quick succession.

sentences.zh: 圭等分兵蹙之，長子縛龍以降，余寇悉平。

translations.literal: Gui and the others divided their forces to press them; Changzi bound Long and surrendered, and the remaining bandits were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Gui split his forces to harry them. Liu Changzi bound Shi Long and submitted, and the remaining rebels were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 錄功，加圭太子少保，增俸一級。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded; Gui was given the additional title Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and one step increase in salary.
translations.idiomatic: When the honors were tallied, Bai Gui was made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and given a raise of one grade.

sentences.zh: 遭父憂，葬畢，視事。

translations.literal: He met with his father's death; when the burial was complete, he resumed office.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he observed mourning, and once the funeral rites were done he returned to duty.

sentences.zh: 三年改兵部尚書，兼督十二團營。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Minister of War and additionally directed the Twelve Corps.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became Minister of War and was put in charge of the Twelve Corps as well.

sentences.zh: 六年，阿羅出等駐牧河套，陜西數被寇。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Aluo Chu and others encamped and pastured in the Ordos; Shaanxi was repeatedly raided.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Aluo Chu and his Mongols settled in the Ordos, and Shaanxi suffered raid after raid.

sentences.zh: 圭言鎮巡官偷肆宜治。

translations.literal: Gui said the frontier defense officials' negligence and laxity ought to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Gui argued that the frontier commanders' negligence deserved punishment.

sentences.zh: 延綏巡撫王銳、鎮守太監秦剛、總兵官房能俱獲罪去。

translations.literal: The Yansui grand coordinator Wang Rui, the garrison eunuch Qin Gang, and the supreme commander Fang Neng were all found guilty and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rui, grand coordinator of Yansui; Qin Gang, the garrison eunuch; and Fang Neng, supreme commander—all were dismissed for their offenses.

sentences.zh: 圭乃議大舉搜河套，發京兵及他鎮兵十萬屯延綏。

translations.literal: Gui then proposed a major sweep of the Ordos, dispatching one hundred thousand metropolitan troops and forces from other garrisons to encamp at Yansui.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Gui then proposed a full-scale campaign to drive the Mongols from the Ordos, mustering a hundred thousand metropolitan and regional troops at Yansui.

sentences.zh: 而以輸餉責河南、山西、陜西民，不給，則預征明年賦。

translations.literal: The burden of supplying provisions was placed on the people of Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi; if they could not pay, next year's taxes were levied in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Supplying the army fell to the people of Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi; those who could not meet the demand had next year's taxes collected ahead of time.

sentences.zh: 於是內地騷然。

translations.literal: Thereupon the interior provinces were in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: The heartland was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 而前後所遣三大將朱永、趙輔、劉聚，皆畏怯不任戰，卒以無功。

translations.literal: Yet the three great generals successively sent—Zhu Yong, Zhao Fu, and Liu Ju—were all timid and unfit for battle, and in the end achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The three commanders dispatched in turn—Zhu Yong, Zhao Fu, and Liu Ju—proved too timid for combat, and the campaign ended in failure.

sentences.zh: 十年卒官，年五十六。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died in office at the age of fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the tenth year, aged fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈少傅，謚恭敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title Junior Mentor, with the posthumous name Gongmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Mentor and given the posthumous name Gongmin, "Reverent and Keen."

sentences.zh: 圭性簡重，公退即閉閣臥，請謁皆不得通。

translations.literal: Gui's nature was austere and dignified; when he left public business he shut his door and lay down, and callers seeking audience could not get through.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Gui was austere and reserved. After office hours he shut himself in and would see no one.

sentences.zh: 在貴州時，有憤中官虐而欲刺之者，誤入圭所。

translations.literal: While in Guizhou, there was one who, enraged at eunuch officials' cruelty, wished to assassinate them and mistakenly entered Gui's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Guizhou, a man enraged by eunuch abuses came to assassinate one of them and blundered into Bai Gui's quarters instead.

sentences.zh: 圭擁衾問之，其人驚曰：「乃吾公耶？」

translations.literal: Gui sat up in his bedding and questioned him; the man startled said, "Are you my lord?
translations.idiomatic: Bai Gui sat up under his covers and questioned him. The man cried out in alarm, "You are my lord?

sentences.zh: 即自刎，不殊，仆於地。

translations.literal: He thereupon cut his own throat; he was not killed, and fell prostrate on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Then he slashed his own throat. The wound was not fatal, and he collapsed on the floor.

sentences.zh: 圭呼燭起視，傅以善藥，遣之。

translations.literal: Gui called for a lamp, rose to examine him, applied good medicine, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Gui had a lamp brought, tended the wound with medicine, and let him go.

sentences.zh: 人服其量。

translations.literal: People admired his magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: All admired his forbearance.

sentences.zh: 次子鉞，字秉德。

translations.literal: His second son Yue, style Bingde.
translations.idiomatic: His second son, Yue, styled Bingde.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，授編修。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was made a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 累官太子少保，禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 習典故，以詞翰稱。

translations.literal: He was versed in precedent and was famed for his literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Well versed in institutional precedent, he was known for his literary skill.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太保，謚文裕。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, with the posthumous name Wenyu.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince and given the posthumous name Wenyu, "Cultured and Generous."

sentences.zh: 張瓚，字宗器，孝感人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zan, style Zongqi, was a man of Xiaogan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zan, styled Zongqi, was from Xiaogan.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in Zhengtong 13.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengtong 13 (1448).

sentences.zh: 授工部主事，遷郎中，歷知太原、寧波二府，有善政。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Works, promoted to director, and successively served as prefect of Taiyuan and Ningbo, with good administration.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a secretary in the Ministry of Works, rose to director, and governed Taiyuan and Ningbo with a record of sound administration.

sentences.zh: 成化初，市舶中官福住貪恣，瓚禁戢其下。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, the maritime trade eunuch Fuzhu was greedy and unrestrained; Zan restrained his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chenghua reign the maritime-trade eunuch Fuzhu ran riot with greed; Zhang Zan reined in his men.

sentences.zh: 住誣瓚於朝，瓚遂列住罪。

translations.literal: Fuzhu slandered Zan at court; Zan thereupon listed Fuzhu's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhu denounced Zhang Zan at court, and Zhang Zan answered by laying out Fuzhu's offenses.

sentences.zh: 住被責，其黨多抵法。

translations.literal: Fuzhu was punished, and many of his partisans were brought to justice.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhu was censured, and many of his associates were punished by law.

sentences.zh: 大臣會薦，遷廣東參政，轉浙江左布政使。

translations.literal: Senior officials jointly recommended him; he was transferred to Guangdong as administrative commissioner and then made Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by senior ministers, he became administrative commissioner of Guangdong and then Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 十年冬，以右副都御史巡撫四川。

translations.literal: In the winter of the tenth year he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the tenth year he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 播州致仕宣慰楊輝言，所屬夭壩幹、灣溪諸寨及重安長官司為生苗竊據，請王師進討。

translations.literal: Yang Hui, the retired Pacification Commissioner of Bozhou, reported that the stockades of Yaobagan, Wanxi, and others under his jurisdiction, together with the Chong'an chief's office, had been seized by raw Miao tribes, and requested imperial troops for a punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hui, the retired Pacification Commissioner of Bozhou, reported that Yaobagan, Wanxi, and other stockades under his jurisdiction, along with the Chong'an chief's domain, had been seized by unsubjugated Miao tribes, and asked for an imperial expedition.

sentences.zh: 詔瓚諭還侵地，不服則征之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zan to instruct them to return the seized lands; if they did not submit, he was to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Zhang Zan to demand the return of the seized territory and to attack if they refused.

sentences.zh: 瓚率兵討定，請設安寧宣撫司，即授輝子友為宣撫以鎮。

translations.literal: Zan led troops to suppress and settle the matter, requested establishment of the Anning Pacification Commission, and immediately appointed Hui's son You as pacification commissioner to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zan led troops to pacify the region, proposed creating the Anning Pacification Commission, and installed Yang Hui's son You as its commissioner.

sentences.zh: 詔可，賜敕獎勞。

translations.literal: The edict approved it, and an imperial letter of commendation and reward was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved and sent an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 以母老乞歸，母已卒。

translations.literal: He requested leave to return on grounds that his mother was old, but his mother had already died.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire to care for his aged mother—only to learn she had already died.

sentences.zh: 會松、茂番寇邊，詔起復視事。

translations.literal: When the Song and Mao tribes raided the frontier, an edict recalled him to service.
translations.idiomatic: When Song and Mao tribes raided the border, the court recalled him from mourning.

sentences.zh: 先是，僉事林璧言：「松茂曩為大鎮。

translations.literal: Earlier, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Lin Bi had said, "Song and Mao were formerly a major garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Lin Bi had argued, "Song and Mao were once a major command.

sentences.zh: 都御史寇深、侍郎羅綺嘗假便宜，專制其地，故有功。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Kou Shen and Vice Minister Luo Qi once exercised discretionary authority and held sole control over the region, and therefore achieved success.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Kou Shen and Vice Minister Luo Qi once held discretionary power over the region and won victories because of it.

sentences.zh: 今惟設兩參將，以副使居中調度。

translations.literal: Now only two regional commanders are posted, with an assistant commissioner coordinating from the center.
translations.idiomatic: Now there are only two regional commanders, with an assistant commissioner mediating between them.

sentences.zh: 事權輕，臨敵稟令制府，千里請戰，謀泄機緩，未有能獲利者。

translations.literal: Their authority is slight; facing the enemy they must request orders from the provincial headquarters—a thousand li to ask permission to fight—plans leak and opportunities slow, and none have been able to gain advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Their authority is too weak: in battle they must petition provincial headquarters a thousand li away for permission to fight. Plans leak, momentum is lost, and no one has profited.

sentences.zh: 宜別置重臣彈壓，或即命瓚兼領，專其責成。」

translations.literal: A heavy minister ought to be separately appointed to suppress the region, or Zan should immediately be ordered to hold concurrent command and bear sole responsibility for success.
translations.idiomatic: A senior official should be posted with full authority, or Zhang Zan should be given concurrent command and held solely accountable.

sentences.zh: 十二年七月命瓚兼督松茂、安綿、建昌軍務。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twelfth year Zan was ordered to concurrently direct military affairs in Song-Mao, Anmian, and Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twelfth year Zhang Zan was put in charge of military affairs in Song-Mao, Anmian, and Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 瓚至軍，審度形勢，改大壩舊設副使於安綿，而令副總兵堯彧軍松潘，參將孫暠軍威、疊，為夾攻計。

translations.literal: When Zan reached the army, he assessed the terrain, moved the former assistant commissioner posted at Daba to Anmian, ordered Vice Commander Yao Yu to garrison Songpan, and Regional Commander Sun Gao to garrison Wei and Die, planning a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the front Zhang Zan studied the terrain, shifted the assistant commissioner formerly at Daba to Anmian, stationed Vice Commander Yao Yu at Songpan and Regional Commander Sun Gao at Wei and Die, and laid plans for a pincer assault.

sentences.zh: 乘間修河西舊路，作浮梁，治月城。

translations.literal: Seizing an interval, he repaired the old west-of-river route, built a pontoon bridge, and restored Moon Fort.
translations.idiomatic: When opportunity allowed he reopened the old west-bank route, built a pontoon bridge, and repaired Moon Fort.

sentences.zh: 避偏橋棧道，軍獲安行，轉餉無阻。

translations.literal: Avoiding the Pianqiao plank road, the army could march safely and supply transport went unimpeded.
translations.idiomatic: By bypassing the treacherous Pianqiao plank road, troops marched safely and supplies moved without hindrance.

sentences.zh: 十四年六月攻白草壩、西坡、禪定數大寨，斬獲亡算。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year he attacked the major stockades of Baicao Dam, Xipo, and Chanding; kills and captures were beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year he stormed the great stockades at Baicao Dam, Xipo, and Chanding, with kills and captures beyond numbering.

sentences.zh: 徇茂州、疊溪，所過降附。

translations.literal: He marched through Maozhou and Diexi; wherever he passed, people submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He swept through Maozhou and Diexi, and every place he passed submitted.

sentences.zh: 抵曲山三寨，攻破之，再討平白草壩余寇。

translations.literal: Reaching the three stockades of Qushan, he broke them; he campaigned again and pacified the remaining bandits of Baicao Dam.
translations.idiomatic: He took the three Qushan stockades by storm, then returned to mop up the remaining rebels at Baicao Dam.

sentences.zh: 先後破滅五十二寨，賊魁撒哈等皆殲。

translations.literal: In succession he destroyed fifty-two stockades; the bandit chiefs Sahha and others were all exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: In all he destroyed fifty-two stockades and wiped out the rebel leaders, including Sahha.

sentences.zh: 他一百五寨悉獻馬納款，諸番盡平。

translations.literal: The other one hundred fifty stockades all presented horses and submitted; all the tribes were fully pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Another hundred and fifty stockades offered horses in submission, and every tribe was pacified.

sentences.zh: 留兵戍要害，增置墩堡，乃班師。

translations.literal: He left troops to garrison strategic points, added beacon towers and forts, and then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: He left garrisons at key points, built new watchtowers and forts, and marched home.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其功，征拜戶部左侍郎，辭歸終制。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his merit, summoned and appointed him Left Vice Minister of Revenue; he declined and returned to complete his mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his achievement and summoned him as Left Vice Minister of Revenue, but he declined and went home to finish mourning.

sentences.zh: 十五年起左副都御史，總督漕運，兼巡撫江北諸府。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was recalled as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, Director-General of Grain Transport, and concurrently grand coordinator of the prefectures north of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was recalled as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, put in charge of Grand Canal transport, and made grand coordinator of the Jiangbei prefectures.

sentences.zh: 十八年，歲大祲，疏請振濟。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, when the year was one of severe famine, he memorialized requesting relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, amid severe famine, he memorialized for relief grain.

sentences.zh: 發銀五萬兩，復敕瓚移淮安倉糧分振，而瓚已卒。

translations.literal: Fifty thousand taels of silver were issued, and an edict again ordered Zan to transfer grain from the Huai'an granaries for distribution in relief—but Zan had already died.
translations.idiomatic: The court released fifty thousand taels of silver and ordered Zhang Zan to distribute grain from the Huai'an granaries—but he had already died.

sentences.zh: 瓚功名著西蜀。

translations.literal: Zan's achievements and reputation were outstanding in western Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zan's reputation in western Sichuan was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 其後撫蜀者如謝士元輩，雖有名，不及瓚。

translations.literal: Later grand coordinators of Shu such as Xie Shiyuan, though they had fame, did not match Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Later governors of Sichuan, men like Xie Shiyuan, enjoyed reputations of their own but never matched Zhang Zan.

sentences.zh: 惟夭壩幹之役，或言楊輝溺愛庶長子友，欲官之，詐言生苗為亂，瓚信而興師，其功不無矯飾雲。

translations.literal: Only in the Yaobagan campaign, some say Yang Hui doted on his eldest son by a concubine, You, wished to give him office, falsely reported raw Miao tribes in revolt; Zan believed it and raised troops—the merit was not without embellishment.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Yaobagan campaign drew criticism: some said Yang Hui, doting on his eldest son by a concubine, You, wanted an office for him and fabricated a Miao rebellion. Zhang Zan believed him and marched—and the victory was not without a touch of stagecraft.

sentences.zh: 謝士元，字仲仁，長樂人。

translations.literal: Xie Shiyuan, style Zhongren, was a man of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shiyuan, styled Zhongren, was from Changle.

sentences.zh: 景泰五年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in Jingtai 5.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Jingtai 5 (1454).

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 督通州倉，陳四弊，屢與監倉宦官忤。

translations.literal: Supervising the Tongzhou granaries, he set forth four abuses and repeatedly clashed with the eunuchs overseeing the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: While supervising the Tongzhou granaries he exposed four abuses and repeatedly crossed the eunuchs who ran them.

sentences.zh: 天順七年擢建昌知府。

translations.literal: In Tianshun 7 he was promoted to prefect of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 7 (1463) he was promoted to prefect of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 地多盜，為軍將所庇。

translations.literal: The region had many bandits, sheltered by military officers.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry was rife, shielded by local commanders.

sentences.zh: 士元以他事持軍將，奸發輒得。

translations.literal: Shiyuan seized military officers on other charges; whenever wrongdoing surfaced he caught it.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shiyuan seized on other offenses to hold the commanders to account, and wrongdoing turned up at every turn.

sentences.zh: 民懷券訟田宅，士元叱曰：「偽也，券今式，而所訟乃二十年事。」

translations.literal: A commoner brought a deed to sue over fields and houses; Shiyuan rebuked him, saying, "It is forged—the deed is in the current format, yet what is sued over is a matter of twenty years ago.
translations.idiomatic: When a man produced a deed to sue over land, Xie Shiyuan snapped, "This is a forgery. Deeds now follow the current format, yet your claim concerns events twenty years past.

sentences.zh: 民驚服，訟為衰止。

translations.literal: The commoner was startled into submission, and lawsuits declined and ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The man was astonished into silence, and litigation dwindled away.

sentences.zh: 考滿，進從三品俸，治府事如故，以憂去。

translations.literal: When his term assessment was complete, he was advanced to junior third-rank salary while continuing to govern the prefecture as before; he left on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of his term he was given junior third-rank pay while continuing to govern; he later left office to mourn.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起知廣信。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was recalled to serve as prefect of Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was recalled as prefect of Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 永豐有銀礦，處州民盜發之，聚數千人。

translations.literal: At Yongfeng there was a silver mine; people of Chuzhou illicitly opened it and gathered several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongfeng a silver mine drew thousands of illicit miners from Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 將士憚其驍廣，不敢剿。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers feared their ferocity and numbers and dared not suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The troops feared their numbers and ferocity and would not move against them.

sentences.zh: 士元勒兵趨之，賊遮刺士元，傷左股。

translations.literal: Shiyuan mustered troops and hastened there; the bandits intercepted and stabbed Shiyuan, wounding his left thigh.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shiyuan led troops against them; the miners ambushed him and wounded his left thigh.

sentences.zh: 裹創力戰，獲其魁，塞礦穴而還。

translations.literal: Binding his wound he fought on with force, captured their leader, sealed the mine shafts, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He bandaged the wound and fought on, took the ringleader, sealed the mine shafts, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 入覲，改永平。

translations.literal: On entering audience he was transferred to Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: After an audience at court he was transferred to Yongping.

sentences.zh: 遭喪不赴。

translations.literal: He met with bereavement and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Bereavement kept him from taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 服闋，擢四川右參政，進右布政使。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was promoted to Right Administrative Commissioner of Sichuan and advanced to Right Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was made Right Administrative Commissioner of Sichuan and then Right Provincial Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年就擢右副都御史，巡撫其地。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi 1 he was immediately promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of that region.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 1 (1488) he was promptly made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 土番大小姓者，將煽亂，士元托行邊，馳詣其地。

translations.literal: The Da and Xiao Yi clans were about to stir up rebellion; Shiyuan, under pretext of a frontier inspection, galloped to their territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Da and Xiao Yi clans were on the verge of revolt. Xie Shiyuan rode to their territory under the pretext of a frontier tour.

sentences.zh: 賊恐，羅拜道左，徐慰遣之。

translations.literal: The rebels were afraid; they lined up bowing along the roadside, and he slowly consoled and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, they lined the road to pay homage; he reassured them and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 歲大祲，流民趨就食。

translations.literal: The year was one of severe famine; refugees flocked seeking food.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of severe famine refugees streamed in seeking food.

sentences.zh: 士元振恤有方，全活者數萬。

translations.literal: Shiyuan had effective methods of relief; tens of thousands were wholly saved.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shiyuan organized relief effectively and saved tens of thousands of lives.

sentences.zh: 明年，坐事下獄。

translations.literal: The next year, on account of an offense he was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was jailed on a charge.

sentences.zh: 事白，遂致仕。

translations.literal: When the matter was cleared he thereupon retired.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was cleared he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 孔鏞，字韶文，長洲人。

translations.literal: Kong Yong, style Shaowen, was a man of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yong, styled Shaowen, was from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 景泰五年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in Jingtai 5.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Jingtai 5 (1454).
