sentences.zh: 知都昌縣，分戶九等以定役，設倉水次，便收斂，民甚賴之。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Duchang, he divided households into nine grades to fix corvée, established granaries at riverside stations to facilitate collection, and the people greatly relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Duchang he ranked households in nine grades to fix corvée labor, set up riverside granaries to ease tax collection, and the people benefited greatly.

sentences.zh: 以弟銘尚寧府郡主，改知連山。

translations.literal: Because his younger brother Ming married the Princess of the Ning Principality, he was transferred to serve as magistrate of Lianshan.
translations.idiomatic: When his younger brother Ming married a princess of the Ning fief, he was transferred to magistrate of Lianshan.

sentences.zh: 瑤、僮出沒鄰境，縣民悉竄。

translations.literal: Yao and Zhuang raided the neighboring borders; the county people all fled and hid.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Zhuang raiders struck the neighboring districts, and the county's people fled en masse.

sentences.zh: 鏞往招之，民驚走。

translations.literal: Yong went to summon them back; the people fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yong went to summon them back, but the people ran in fear.

sentences.zh: 鏞炊飯民舍，留錢償其直以去。

translations.literal: Yong cooked a meal in a commoner's house, left money to pay its cost, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He cooked a meal in a villager's home, left money to pay for it, and went on.

sentences.zh: 民乃漸知親鏞，相率還。

translations.literal: The people then gradually came to know and trust Yong, and returned in groups.
translations.idiomatic: Gradually the people came to trust him and returned in groups.

sentences.zh: 鏞慰勞振恤，俾復故業，教以戰守。

translations.literal: Yong consoled and relieved them, enabled them to resume their former livelihoods, and taught them defense in war.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yong comforted them, gave relief, helped them resume their livelihoods, and trained them in defense.

sentences.zh: 道路漸通，縣治遂復。

translations.literal: Roads gradually reopened, and county administration was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Roads reopened one by one, and the county seat was restored.

sentences.zh: 都御史葉盛征廣西，以鏞從。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Ye Sheng campaigned in Guangxi and took Yong to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor-in-Chief Ye Sheng led a campaign in Guangxi, Kong Yong accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 諸將妄殺者，鏞輒力爭，所全活甚眾。

translations.literal: Whenever generals killed wantonly, Yong always argued strenuously; those he thus spared were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever generals killed indiscriminately, Yong argued against it and saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 成化元年，用葉盛等薦，擢高州試知府。

translations.literal: In Chenghua 1, on recommendation of Ye Sheng and others, he was promoted to acting prefect of Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 1 (1465), on the recommendation of Ye Sheng and others, he was appointed acting prefect of Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 前知府劉海以瑤警，閉城門自護。

translations.literal: The former prefect Liu Hai, on Yao alarm, closed the city gates to protect himself.
translations.idiomatic: The previous prefect, Liu Hai, had shut the city gates to protect himself when Yao raiders threatened.

sentences.zh: 鄉民避瑤至者輒不納，還為瑤所戕。

translations.literal: When country folk fleeing the Yao arrived he would not admit them, and they were in turn slain by the Yao.
translations.idiomatic: When villagers fleeing the Yao reached the gates he refused them entry, and they were killed by the raiders instead.

sentences.zh: 又疑民陰附賊，輒戮之。

translations.literal: He also suspected the people of secretly siding with the bandits and would execute them.
translations.idiomatic: He also suspected civilians of secretly aiding the rebels and had them executed.

sentences.zh: 賊緣是激眾怒，為內應，城遂陷。

translations.literal: The bandits thereby stirred the people's wrath and served as inside collaborators, and the city then fell.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels exploited this to incite popular anger, found inside help, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 鏞至，開門納來者，流亡日歸。

translations.literal: When Yong arrived, he opened the gates and admitted those who came; exiles returned day by day.
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Yong arrived he opened the gates to refugees, and exiles returned day by day.

sentences.zh: 城不能容，別築城東北居之。

translations.literal: The city could not accommodate them, so he built another city northeast to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: The city could not hold everyone, so he built a new settlement northeast of the wall.

sentences.zh: 附郭多暴骸，民以疫死，復為義冢瘞焉。

translations.literal: Outside the suburbs many corpses lay exposed; people died of pestilence, and he again had communal burial mounds built to inter them.
translations.idiomatic: Unburied corpses lay outside the suburbs where plague had killed many; he had charity tombs built to bury them.

sentences.zh: 時賊屯境內者凡十余部，而其魁馮曉屯化州，鄧公長屯茅峒，屢招不就。

translations.literal: At the time more than ten bandit bands were encamped within the border; their chiefs Feng Xiao held Huazhou and Deng Gongchang held Maodong, and though repeatedly summoned they would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten rebel bands were camped within the prefecture. Their leaders, Feng Xiao at Huazhou and Deng Gongchang at Maodong, had been summoned repeatedly without submitting.

sentences.zh: 鏞一日單騎從二人直抵茅峒。

translations.literal: One day Yong rode alone with only two attendants straight to Maodong.
translations.idiomatic: One day Kong Yong rode alone to Maodong with only two companions.

sentences.zh: 峒去城十里許，道遇賊徒，令還告曰：「我新太守也。」

translations.literal: The dong was about ten li from the city; on the road he met bandit followers and had them return and report: "I am the new prefect."
translations.idiomatic: Maodong lay about ten li from the city. On the road he met bandits and sent them back with word: "Tell your chief—the new prefect has come.

sentences.zh: 公長驟聞新守至，亟呼其黨擐甲迎。

translations.literal: Gongchang suddenly heard the new prefect had arrived and hastily called his followers to arm themselves and go out to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Gongchang heard the new prefect had arrived and hurriedly summoned his men, fully armed, to meet him.

sentences.zh: 及見鏞坦易無騶從，氣大沮。

translations.literal: When he saw Yong easy and unassuming without mounted escort, his spirits fell greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw Kong Yong plain and unarmed, with no mounted escort, his fighting spirit collapsed.

sentences.zh: 鏞徐下馬，入坐庭中，公長率其徒馳甲羅拜。

translations.literal: Yong slowly dismounted, entered, and sat in the courtyard; Gongchang led his followers in full armor to surround him and bow in a ring.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yong dismounted slowly, walked into the courtyard, and sat down. Gongchang led his armored followers to surround him and kowtow in a ring.

sentences.zh: 鏞諭曰：「汝曹故良民，迫凍餒耳。

translations.literal: Yong instructed them, saying: "You lot were originally good people, forced by cold and hunger alone.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yong addressed them: "You were once law-abiding people, driven to this by hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 前守欲兵汝，吾今奉命為汝父母。

translations.literal: The former prefect wanted to use troops against you; I now receive orders to be your parents.
translations.idiomatic: The last prefect meant to use force against you; I am ordered to be a father and mother to you.

sentences.zh: 汝，我子也。

translations.literal: You are my sons.
translations.idiomatic: You are my children.

sentences.zh: 信我，則送我歸，賚汝粟帛。

translations.literal: If you trust me, then escort me back and I will grant you grain and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Trust me, escort me home, and I will give you grain and cloth.

sentences.zh: 不信，則殺我，即大軍至，無遺種矣。」

translations.literal: If you do not trust me, then kill me; at once the great army will arrive and not one seed will remain."
translations.idiomatic: If you do not trust me, kill me—but then the army will come and leave no one alive.

sentences.zh: 公長猶豫，其黨皆感悟泣下。

translations.literal: Gongchang hesitated; his followers all were moved to understanding and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchang wavered; his followers were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 鏞曰：「餒矣，當食我。」

translations.literal: Yong said: "I am hungry; you ought to feed me."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yong said: "I'm hungry. You should feed me.

sentences.zh: 公長為跪上酒饌。

translations.literal: Gongchang knelt and presented wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchang knelt and served him wine and food.

sentences.zh: 既食，曰：「日且暮，當止宿。」

translations.literal: After eating he said: "The day is near dusk; I ought to stay the night."
translations.idiomatic: After the meal he said: "It's getting late. I should stay the night.

sentences.zh: 夜解衣酣寢。

translations.literal: At night he removed his clothes and slept deeply.
translations.idiomatic: That night he undressed and slept soundly.

sentences.zh: 賊相顧駭服。

translations.literal: The bandits looked at one another in awe and submission.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits exchanged looks, stunned and subdued.

sentences.zh: 再宿而返。

translations.literal: After two nights' lodging he returned.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed two nights, then returned.

sentences.zh: 見道旁裸而懸樹上者累累，詢之，皆諸生也，命盡釋之。

translations.literal: He saw along the road many naked and hanging from trees; on inquiry they were all scholars, and he ordered them all released.
translations.idiomatic: Along the road he saw many naked bodies hung from trees—all scholars, he learned—and ordered them cut down and freed.

sentences.zh: 公長遣數十騎擁還，城中人望見，皆大驚，謂知府被執，來紿降也，盡登陴。

translations.literal: Gongchang sent several dozen horsemen to escort him back; people in the city saw this and were all greatly alarmed, thinking the prefect had been seized and this was a feigned surrender, and all mounted the battlements.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchang sent dozens of horsemen to escort him back. Those on the walls saw them and panicked, thinking the prefect had been captured and this was a ruse to draw them out; they manned the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 鏞止騎城外，獨與羸卒入，取谷帛，使載歸。

translations.literal: Yong halted his horsemen outside the city and entered alone with a few weak soldiers, took grain and cloth, and had it loaded and brought back.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yong left the cavalry outside, entered with a small escort, loaded grain and cloth, and sent it back with them.

sentences.zh: 公長益感激，遂焚其巢，率黨數千人來降。

translations.literal: Gongchang was all the more grateful, then burned their lair and led several thousand followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchang was deeply moved, burned his stronghold, and led several thousand followers to surrender.

sentences.zh: 公長既降，諸賊次第納款，惟曉恃險不服。

translations.literal: Once Gongchang had surrendered, the other bandits successively submitted pledges of allegiance; only Xiao relied on rugged terrain and would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: After Gongchang submitted, other bands surrendered in turn; only Feng Xiao, safe in rough terrain, refused.

sentences.zh: 鏞選壯士二百人，乘夜抵化州。

translations.literal: Yong selected two hundred stalwart men and under cover of night reached Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yong picked two hundred stalwart men and reached Huazhou by night.

sentences.zh: 曉倉皇走匿，獲其妻子以歸，撫恤甚厚，曉亦以五百人降。

translations.literal: Xiao fled in panic and hid; Yong captured his wife and children and returned, treated them very generously, and Xiao also surrendered with five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xiao fled in panic. Kong Yong took his wife and children, treated them kindly, and Xiao surrendered with five hundred followers.

sentences.zh: 已，與僉事陶魯敗賊廖婆保。

translations.literal: Thereafter, together with Assistant Commissioner Tao Lu he defeated the bandit Liaopobao.
translations.idiomatic: He and Assistant Commissioner Tao Lu then defeated the rebel Liaopobao.

sentences.zh: 他賊先後來犯，多敗去。

translations.literal: Other bandits came to attack one after another and were mostly defeated and driven off.
translations.idiomatic: Other rebels attacked in succession and were mostly beaten back.

sentences.zh: 境內大定。

translations.literal: Within the border was largely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture was largely pacified.

sentences.zh: 上官交薦，擢按察副使，分巡高、雷二府。

translations.literal: Superiors recommended him in turn; he was promoted to Assistant Surveillance Commissioner and assigned to circuit Gaozhou and Leizhou prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: His superiors recommended him repeatedly; he was promoted to Assistant Surveillance Commissioner with jurisdiction over Gaozhou and Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 益招劇賊染定、侯大六、鄧辛酉等，給田產，分處內地為官，備他盜。

translations.literal: He further recruited fierce bandits Ran Ding, Hou Dalu, Deng Xinyou, and others, granted them fields and estates, stationed them inland as officials, and prepared against other bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited more hardened rebels—Ran Ding, Hou Dalu, Deng Xinyou, and others—granted them land, resettled them inland as local officials, and used them against other bandits.

sentences.zh: 廣西賊犯信宜、岑溪，皆擊敗之。

translations.literal: Guangxi bandits invaded Xinyi and Cenxi; he defeated them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangxi rebels raided Xinyi and Cenxi he defeated them all.

sentences.zh: 治績聞，賜誥命旌異。

translations.literal: His administrative achievements became known; he was granted an imperial patent of commendation and special distinction.
translations.idiomatic: His record reached the throne; he received an imperial commendation and special honors.

sentences.zh: 遭喪，服除，改廣西。

translations.literal: He suffered bereavement; when mourning ended he was transferred to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: After a bereavement and the end of mourning he was transferred to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 瑤、僮聞鏞至，悉遠循。

translations.literal: When the Yao and Zhuang heard Yong had arrived, they all fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: At word that Kong Yong had arrived, Yao and Zhuang raiders fled the region.

sentences.zh: 十四年，兵部上其功，賚銀幣，尋進按察使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the Ministry of War reported his achievements; he was granted silver and silk coins, and soon promoted to Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen the Ministry of War reported his achievements; he received silver and silk rewards and was soon promoted to Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 荔浦賊來寇，總督朱英以兵屬鏞，擊平之，進食二品祿。

translations.literal: Lipu bandits came to raid; Governor Zhu Ying entrusted troops to Yong, who attacked and pacified them, and was advanced to second-rank stipend.
translations.idiomatic: When Lipu rebels raided, Governor Zhu Ying put troops under Kong Yong, who crushed them and was granted second-rank stipend.

sentences.zh: 已，遷左布政使。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was transferred to Left Administrative Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Left Administrative Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 旋以右副都御史巡撫貴州。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 清平部苗阿溪者，桀驁多智。

translations.literal: Among the Miao of Qingping was one Axi, fierce, defiant, and very clever.
translations.idiomatic: Axi, a Miao chieftain of the Qingping region, was fierce, proud, and cunning.

sentences.zh: 其養子阿賴尤有力，橫行諸部中，守臣皆納溪賂，驕不可制。

translations.literal: His adopted son Alai was especially powerful, rampaging through the various tribes; border officials all accepted Axi's bribes, and he was arrogant beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: His adopted son Alai was especially strong and terrorized neighboring tribes. Local officials took Axi's bribes; he was too proud to control.

sentences.zh: 鏞行部至清平，詢得溪所昵者二人。

translations.literal: Yong on inspection tour reached Qingping, inquired, and learned two men whom Axi favored.
translations.idiomatic: On an inspection tour to Qingping, Kong Yong learned who Axi's two closest confidants were.

sentences.zh: 遂以計擒溪，磔之，並討平雞背苗，郡蠻震懾。

translations.literal: He then by stratagem captured Axi, dismembered him, and together suppressed the Jibeimiao; the tribes of the commandery were awed.
translations.idiomatic: By stratagem he captured Axi and executed him by dismemberment, crushed the Jibeimiao as well, and the tribes of the region were shaken into submission.

sentences.zh: 鏞居官廉。

translations.literal: Yong in office was incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yong served with integrity.

sentences.zh: 歷仕三十余年，皆在邊陲，觸瘴成疾。

translations.literal: Over more than thirty years of office he was always on the frontier; he contracted miasma illness and fell sick.
translations.idiomatic: For more than thirty years he served on the frontier, contracted miasmal illness, and fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 乞骸骨，不許。

translations.literal: He begged leave to retire; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to retire but was refused.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年召為工部右侍郎，道卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi 2 he was summoned as Right Vice Minister of Works; on the road he died, age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 2 (1489) he was summoned as Right Vice Minister of Works but died on the journey at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 平樂李時敏者，為信宜知縣。

translations.literal: Li Shimin of Pingle served as magistrate of Xinyi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin of Pingle was magistrate of Xinyi.

sentences.zh: 嘗與鏞共平瑤亂，有功，遷知化州。

translations.literal: He once together with Yong pacified Yao unrest and had merit; he was transferred to administer Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He had helped Kong Yong quell Yao unrest with distinction and was transferred to prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 粵人以孔李並稱。

translations.literal: People of Guangdong spoke of Kong and Li together.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangdong, Kong and Li were spoken of in the same breath.

sentences.zh: 鄧廷瓚，字宗器，巴陵人。

translations.literal: Deng Tingzan, style Zongqi, was a man of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Tingzan, styled Zongqi, was from Baling.

sentences.zh: 景泰五年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in Jingtai 5.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Jingtai 5 (1454).

sentences.zh: 知淳安縣，有惠政。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Chun'an he had benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Chun'an he governed with benevolence.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服除，遷太仆寺丞。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his mother; when mourning ended he was transferred to Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he was appointed Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 貴州新設程番府，地在萬山中，蠻僚雜居，吏部難其人，特擢廷瓚為知府。

translations.literal: Guizhou newly established Chenfan Prefecture; the place lay amid myriad mountains with mixed Miao and Liao settlement; the Ministry of Personnel found it hard to find the right man and specially promoted Tingzan as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenfan Prefecture was newly established in Guizhou—deep in the mountains, with mixed tribal settlement—the Ministry of Personnel could find no suitable appointee and specially promoted Deng Tingzan to prefect.

sentences.zh: 至則悉心規畫，城郭、衢巷、學校、壇廟、廨舍，以次興建。

translations.literal: On arrival he devoted himself to planning; city walls and gates, streets and lanes, schools, ritual altars and temples, and official quarters were built up in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he planned carefully; walls, streets, schools, temples, and government offices were built in turn.

sentences.zh: 榜諭諸僚受約束。

translations.literal: He posted proclamations instructing the various tribes to accept regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He posted notices requiring the tribes to submit to law.

sentences.zh: 政平令和。

translations.literal: Government was calm and orders harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: The region grew peaceful and orderly.

sentences.zh: 巡撫陳儼上其治行。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Chen Yan reported his administrative conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Chen Yan reported his excellent governance to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝令久任。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to serve long in the post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him retained in office.

sentences.zh: 九載秩滿，始遷山東左參政，尋進右布政使。

translations.literal: After nine years when his term expired he was first transferred to Left Assistant Commissioner of Shandong, then soon promoted to Right Administrative Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years, when his term ended, he was transferred to Left Assistant Commissioner in Shandong and soon promoted to Right Administrative Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年以右副都御史巡撫貴州。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi 2 he became Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 2 (1489) he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 廷瓚自令至守，淹常調者逾三十年。

translations.literal: From magistrate to prefect, Tingzan remained in regular appointments for more than thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: From county magistrate to prefect, Deng Tingzan had lingered in routine postings for more than thirty years.

sentences.zh: 至是去知府止三歲，遂得開府。

translations.literal: Only after leaving the prefecture for three years did he at last obtain the grand coordinator's seal.
translations.idiomatic: Only three years after leaving the prefecture did he at last receive a grand coordinator's commission.

sentences.zh: 以生母憂歸。

translations.literal: On bereavement for his birth mother he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to mourn his birth mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，還原任。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he returned to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he resumed his former post.

sentences.zh: 都勻苗乜富架、長腳等作亂，敕廷瓚提督軍務，同湖廣總兵官顧溥、貴州總兵官王通等討之。

translations.literal: Duyun Miao Mi Fujia, Changjiao, and others rebelled; the emperor ordered Tingzan to take overall charge of military affairs and together with Huguang Regional Commander Gu Pu, Guizhou Regional Commander Wang Tong, and others suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When Duyun Miao chieftains Mi Fujia and Changjiao rebelled, the emperor put Deng Tingzan in charge of the campaign, with Regional Commanders Gu Pu of Huguang and Wang Tong of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 副使吳倬遣熟苗詐降富架，誘令入寇，伏兵擒其父子。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Wu Zhuo sent trusted Miao to feign surrender to Fujia, lured him to raid, and with hidden troops captured father and son.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Wu Zhuo sent allied Miao to feign surrender to Fujia, lure him into an attack, and ambush him—capturing father and son.

sentences.zh: 官軍乘勝連破百余寨，生系長腳以歸，群蠻震懾。

translations.literal: Government troops pressing the advantage broke more than a hundred stockades in succession, took Changjiao alive and brought him back, and the tribal groups were awed.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops pressed the advantage, took more than a hundred stockades in succession, captured Changjiao alive, and the tribes were shaken into submission.

sentences.zh: 廷瓚言：「都勻；

translations.literal: Tingzan said: "Duyun;
translations.idiomatic: Deng Tingzan memorialized: "In Duyun—

sentences.zh: 清平舊設二衛、九長官司，其人皆世祿，自用其法，恣虐，激變苗民，亂四十余年。

translations.literal: Qingping formerly had two guards and nine native chieftainships established; their people all held hereditary stipends, applied their own laws as they pleased, tyrannized and abused, incited the Miao to revolt, and there was disorder for more than forty years.
translations.idiomatic: Qingping formerly had two guard posts and nine native chieftainships whose officers held hereditary stipends, applied their own law as they pleased, abused the people, and stirred Miao revolt for more than forty years.

sentences.zh: 今元兇就除，非大更張不可。

translations.literal: Now that the chief culprit has been removed, nothing less than a great overhaul will do.
translations.idiomatic: With the ringleaders gone, nothing less than sweeping reform will suffice.

sentences.zh: 請改為府縣，設流官與土官兼治，庶可久安。」

translations.literal: He requested converting to prefecture and counties, establishing both regular officials and native chiefs to govern jointly, so that long peace might be achieved."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed converting the region into prefectures and counties under both regular and native officials so peace might last.

sentences.zh: 因上善後十一事，帝悉從之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted eleven items on good administration thereafter; the emperor approved them all.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted eleven reforms for pacification; the emperor approved them all.

sentences.zh: 遂設府一，曰都勻，州二，曰獨山、麻哈；

translations.literal: Thereupon one prefecture was established, called Duyun, and two subprefectures, called Dushan and Maha;
translations.idiomatic: One prefecture was set up, Duyun; two subprefectures, Dushan and Maha;

sentences.zh: 縣一，曰清平。

translations.literal: one county, called Qingping.
translations.idiomatic: and one county, Qingping.

sentences.zh: 苗患自此漸戢。

translations.literal: Miao troubles from this gradually subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Miao unrest gradually subsided thereafter.

sentences.zh: 論功，進右都御史。

translations.literal: On merit reckoning he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 八年召掌南京都察院事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was summoned to direct the Nanjing Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he was summoned to head the Nanjing Censorate.

sentences.zh: 甫數月，命提督兩廣軍務兼巡撫。

translations.literal: After only several months he was ordered to take overall charge of military affairs in the Two Guangs and concurrently serve as Grand Coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Only months later he was ordered to command military affairs in the Two Guangs and serve as Grand Coordinator.

sentences.zh: 越二年，進左。

translations.literal: After two years he was promoted to Left [Censor-in-Chief].
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 廷瓚治尚簡易，於吏事但總大綱，結群蠻以恩信，不輕用兵，而兵出必成功。

translations.literal: Tingzan in governing favored simplicity and ease; in official business he only held the general outline; he bound the tribal groups with grace and trust, did not lightly use troops, yet when troops went out they always succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Tingzan governed with simplicity, grasping only the broad outlines of administration. He won tribal allegiance through grace and trust, avoided force when he could, and yet every campaign succeeded.

sentences.zh: 郁林、雲壚、大桂諸蠻及四會饑民作亂，以次討平，兩廣遂無事。

translations.literal: Yulin, Yunqiu, Dagui, and other tribes and Sihui starving people rebelled; he suppressed them in sequence, and the Two Guangs were then untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellions by the tribes of Yulin, Yunqiu, and Dagui and by famine-driven people in Sihui were crushed in turn, and the Two Guangs were pacified.

sentences.zh: 十三年復召掌南院。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was again summoned to direct the Southern Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirteen he was again summoned to head the Southern Censorate.

sentences.zh: 未行，卒。

translations.literal: Before he could go, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post he died.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚襄敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; posthumous title Xiangmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Xiangmin.

sentences.zh: 廷瓚有雅量，待人不疑，時多稱其長者。

translations.literal: Tingzan had generous forbearance, treated people without suspicion, and his contemporaries often praised him as an elder of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Tingzan was magnanimous and trusting; contemporaries often praised his forbearance.

sentences.zh: 至所設施，動中機宜。

translations.literal: As for what he established and carried out, his measures always hit the critical point.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what he enacted always struck the mark.

sentences.zh: 其在貴州平苗功為尤偉雲。

translations.literal: His achievement in pacifying the Miao in Guizhou was especially great—so it is said.
translations.idiomatic: His pacification of the Miao in Guizhou was his greatest achievement of all.

sentences.zh: 王軾，字用敬，公安人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi, style Yongjing, was a man of Gong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi, styled Yongjing, was from Gong'an.

sentences.zh: 天順八年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in Tianshun 8.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Tianshun 8 (1464).

sentences.zh: 授大理右評事，遷右寺正。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Reviewing Officer of the Court of Judicial Review, then transferred to Right Assistant Director of the Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Reviewing Officer of the Court of Judicial Review and later promoted to Right Assistant Director of the Court.

sentences.zh: 錄囚四川，平反百余人，擢四川副使。

translations.literal: Reviewing prisoners in Sichuan, he reversed wrongful convictions for more than a hundred people and was promoted to Sichuan Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: While reviewing prisoners in Sichuan, he overturned more than a hundred wrongful convictions and was promoted to Vice Commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 歲兇，請官銀十萬兩為糴費。

translations.literal: In a year of famine, he requested one hundred thousand taels of official silver for grain-purchase funds.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck, he requested one hundred thousand taels of government silver for grain purchases.

sentences.zh: 以按嘉定同知盛崇仁贓罪，被訐下吏。

translations.literal: Because in investigating the corruption of Jiading Vice Magistrate Sheng Chongren he was denounced, he was handed over to the judicial authorities.
translations.idiomatic: While investigating corruption charges against Sheng Chongren, Vice Magistrate of Jiading, he was denounced and turned over to the judicial authorities.

sentences.zh: 事白，還職，改陜西。

translations.literal: When the matter was cleared, he returned to his post and was transferred to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Once the matter was cleared, he was restored to office and transferred to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，擢四川按察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Hongzhi reign, he was promoted to Sichuan Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Hongzhi reign, he was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 三年遷南京右僉都御史，提督操江。

translations.literal: In year three he was transferred to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing and put in charge of the Yangtze patrol fleet.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 3 (1490) he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing and placed in charge of the Yangtze patrol fleet.

sentences.zh: 八年進右副都御史，總理南京糧儲，旋命巡撫貴州。

translations.literal: In year eight he was advanced to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, took overall charge of Nanjing grain reserves, and soon afterward was ordered to serve as Grand Coordinator of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 8 (1495) he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief to oversee Nanjing grain reserves, and was soon afterward appointed Grand Coordinator of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 明年入為大理卿，詔與刑部裁定條例頒天下。

translations.literal: The next year he entered the capital as Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review; an edict ordered him together with the Ministry of Justice to fix regulations and promulgate them throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he entered the capital as Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review. An edict ordered him and the Ministry of Justice to finalize legal regulations and promulgate them empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 十三年拜南京戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In year thirteen he was appointed Minister of Revenue at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 13 (1500) he was appointed Minister of Revenue at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 尋命兼左副都御史，督貴州軍務，討普安賊婦米魯。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered additionally to serve as Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief, supervise Guizhou military affairs, and suppress the bandit woman Milu of Pu'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered also to serve as Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief, supervise military affairs in Guizhou, and suppress the bandit leader Milu of Pu'an.

sentences.zh: 時鎮守中官楊友、總兵官曹愷、巡撫錢鉞共發兵討魯，大敗於阿馬坡。

translations.literal: At the time the resident eunuch commissioner Yang You, regional commander Cao Kai, and Grand Coordinator Qian Yue jointly raised troops to suppress Milu and suffered a great defeat at Amapo.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the resident eunuch Yang You, regional commander Cao Kai, and Grand Coordinator Qian Yue jointly marched against Milu and suffered a crushing defeat at Amapo.

sentences.zh: 都指揮吳遠被執，普安幾陷。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Wu Yuan was captured, and Pu'an nearly fell.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Wu Yuan was captured, and Pu'an nearly fell.

sentences.zh: 友等請濟師，乃以命軾。

translations.literal: You and the others requested reinforcements, and the command was therefore given to Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang You and the others requested reinforcements, and Wang Zhi was given the command.

sentences.zh: 軾未至，而友等遣人招賊。

translations.literal: Before Zhi arrived, You and the others sent men to summon the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wang Zhi arrived, Yang You and his colleagues sent envoys to negotiate with the bandits.

sentences.zh: 賊揚言欲降，益擁眾攻圍普安、安南衛城，斷盤江道，勢愈熾。

translations.literal: The bandits proclaimed that they wished to surrender, yet gathered more followers and attacked and besieged the cities of Pu'an and Annan Guard, cut the Pan River route, and their power grew ever fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits claimed they wished to surrender, but instead gathered more followers, besieged Pu'an and Annan Guard, cut the Pan River route, and grew ever bolder.

sentences.zh: 又乘間劫執友。

translations.literal: They also seized an opportunity to capture You by force.
translations.idiomatic: They also seized an opportunity to capture Yang You.

sentences.zh: 右布政使閭鉦，按察使劉福，都指揮李宗武、郭仁、史韜、李雄、吳達等死焉。

translations.literal: Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Lu Zheng, Surveillance Commissioner Liu Fu, and Regional Commanders Li Zongwu, Guo Ren, Shi Tao, Li Xiong, Wu Da, and others died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Lu Zheng, Surveillance Commissioner Liu Fu, and Regional Commanders Li Zongwu, Guo Ren, Shi Tao, Li Xiong, Wu Da, and others were killed.

sentences.zh: 軾至，以便宜調廣西、湖廣、雲南、四川官軍、土兵八萬人，合貴州兵，分八道進，使致仕都督王通將一軍。

translations.literal: When Zhi arrived, by discretionary authority he mobilized eighty thousand regular and native troops from Guangxi, Huguang, Yunnan, and Sichuan, combined them with Guizhou forces, divided them into eight columns to advance, and had retired Chief Commander Wang Tong lead one army.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhi arrived, he exercised discretionary authority to mobilize eighty thousand regular and native troops from Guangxi, Huguang, Yunnan, and Sichuan, combined them with Guizhou forces, divided them into eight columns, and put retired Chief Commander Wang Tong in command of one army.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月，參將趙晟破六墜寨。

translations.literal: In the first month of year fifteen, Assistant Commander Zhao Sheng captured Liuzhui Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Hongzhi 15 (1502), Assistant Commander Zhao Sheng captured Liuzhui Stockade.

sentences.zh: 賊遁，過盤江。

translations.literal: The bandits fled and crossed the Pan River.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits fled across the Pan River.

sentences.zh: 都指揮張泰等渡江追擊，指揮劉懷等遂進解安南衛圍，而愷、通及都指揮李政亦各破賊寨。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Zhang Tai and others crossed the river in pursuit; Commander Liu Huai and others then advanced and lifted the siege of Annan Guard, while Kai, Tong, and Regional Commander Li Zheng each also broke bandit stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Zhang Tai and others crossed the river in pursuit; Commander Liu Huai and others advanced and lifted the siege of Annan Guard, while Cao Kai, Wang Tong, and Regional Commander Li Zheng each captured bandit stockades as well.

sentences.zh: 賊還攻平夷衛及大河、扼勒諸堡，都御史陳金以雲南兵禦之。

translations.literal: The bandits turned back to attack Pingyi Guard and the forts of Dahe, Ele, and others; Censor-in-Chief Chen Jin repelled them with Yunnan troops.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits turned back to attack Pingyi Guard and the forts at Dahe, Ele, and elsewhere; Censor-in-Chief Chen Jin repelled them with Yunnan troops.

sentences.zh: 賊遁歸馬尾籠寨。

translations.literal: The bandits fled back to Maweilong Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits retreated to Maweilong Stockade.

sentences.zh: 官軍聚攻益急，土官鳳英等格殺米魯，余黨遂平。

translations.literal: Government troops pressed the attack ever more fiercely; native official Feng Ying and others killed Milu in combat, and the remaining followers were then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops pressed the attack ever harder; native official Feng Ying and others killed Milu in battle, and the remaining bandits were pacified.

sentences.zh: 用兵凡五月，破賊寨千余，斬首四千八百有奇，俘獲一千二百。

translations.literal: Troops were employed for five months in all; more than a thousand bandit stockades were taken, heads cut numbered more than four thousand eight hundred, and captives numbered one thousand two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign lasted five months. More than a thousand bandit stockades were captured, nearly four thousand eight hundred heads were taken, and twelve hundred prisoners were seized.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，帝大喜，嘉勞。

translations.literal: When news of victory arrived, the emperor was greatly pleased and rewarded them with commendation.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory arrived, the emperor was greatly pleased and issued rewards and commendations.

sentences.zh: 召還京，賜賚有加，錄功，加太子少保。

translations.literal: He was summoned back to the capital, granted additional gifts, his merit was recorded, and he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital, richly rewarded, and his merit recorded with promotion to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 已，改南京兵部，參贊機務。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was transferred to the Ministry of War at Nanjing and participated in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to the Ministry of War at Nanjing to participate in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 連乞致仕，不允。

translations.literal: He repeatedly requested retirement, but it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly requested retirement, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，遇疾復請。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong acceded, he fell ill and again made the request.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong acceded to the throne, he fell ill and again requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 詔加太子太保。

translations.literal: An edict added the title Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted him to Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 賜敕乘傳歸。

translations.literal: He was granted an imperial letter and allowed to return home by post relay.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted an imperial letter and allowed to return home by official relay.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太保，謚襄簡。

translations.literal: He died; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian and given the posthumous title Xiangjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Grand Guardian with the posthumous name Xiangjian.

sentences.zh: 劉丙，字文煥，南雄知府實孫也。

translations.literal: Liu Bing, style Wenhuan, was the grandson of Nanxiong Prefect Liu Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bing, styled Wenhuan, was the grandson of Liu Shi, Prefect of Nanxiong.

sentences.zh: 成化末，登進士。

translations.literal: At the end of the Chenghua reign he attained jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Chenghua reign he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，改御史，巡按雲南。

translations.literal: Selected as a Hanlin bachelor, he was transferred to censor and sent on an inspection tour of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a Hanlin bachelor, he was transferred to censor and sent to inspect Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 雲南諸司吏，舊不得給由，父滿子代，丙請如例考入官。

translations.literal: Clerks of the various offices in Yunnan had formerly not been granted certificates of appointment; when a father completed his term a son replaced him. Bing requested that, according to precedent, they be allowed to enter office through examination.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks in Yunnan's local offices had long been denied formal certificates of appointment, with sons succeeding fathers when terms expired. Liu Bing petitioned that they be allowed to enter office through examination, as elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 流戍僉發，必經兵部，多淹延致死。

translations.literal: For exiles sent to frontier garrison duty, dispatch had to pass through the Ministry of War, and many died from prolonged delay.
translations.idiomatic: Exiles sent to frontier garrison duty had to be processed through the Ministry of War, and many died from the delays.

sentences.zh: 丙請屬之撫、按。

translations.literal: Bing requested that authority be vested in the grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bing petitioned that authority over such cases be vested in the grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners.

sentences.zh: 土官無後者，請錄其弟侄，勿令妻妾冒冠服。

translations.literal: For native officials without heirs, he requested that younger brothers and nephews be registered in succession, and that wives and concubines not be allowed to usurp official caps and robes.
translations.idiomatic: Where native officials left no heirs, he petitioned that younger brothers and nephews be registered as successors, and that wives and concubines not be allowed to assume official rank and regalia.

sentences.zh: 俱著為例。

translations.literal: All were established as precedents.
translations.idiomatic: All of these proposals were established as precedent.

sentences.zh: 後督兩淮鹽課，中官請引二萬為織造費，部議許之，丙執不可，得減四之三。

translations.literal: Later, while supervising the salt tax of the Two Huai regions, a eunuch requested twenty thousand salt certificates for weaving expenses; the ministry deliberated and approved, but Bing firmly refused, and the amount was reduced by three-fourths.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while supervising the Two Huai salt tax, a eunuch requested twenty thousand salt certificates to fund imperial weaving. The ministry approved, but Liu Bing firmly objected, and the amount was cut by three-fourths.

sentences.zh: 歷福建、四川副使，俱督學校，三遷四川左布政使。

translations.literal: He served successively as Vice Commissioner in Fujian and Sichuan, in both posts supervising schools, and after three promotions became Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Commissioner in Fujian and Sichuan, supervising schools in both posts, and after three promotions became Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 正德六年以右副都御史巡撫湖廣。

translations.literal: In Zhengde 6 he was appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 6 (1511) he was appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 所部鎮溪千戶所、筸子坪長官司與貴州銅仁，四川酉陽、梅桐諸土司，犬牙相錯。

translations.literal: Within his jurisdiction, Zhenxi Guard Battalion, Ganziping Native Official Office, Tongren in Guizhou, and the native chieftaincies of Youyang and Meitong in Sichuan interlocked like dogs' teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Within his jurisdiction, Zhenxi Guard Battalion, Ganziping Native Official Office, Tongren in Guizhou, and the native chieftaincies of Youyang and Meitong in Sichuan interlocked in a tangled borderland.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，錯溪苗龍麻陽與銅仁苗龍童保聚眾攻剽，土官李樁等實縱之，而筸子百夫長龍真與通謀。

translations.literal: During the Hongzhi reign, the Miao Long Mayang of Cuoxi and the Miao Long Tongbao of Tongren gathered followers to raid and plunder; native officials such as Li Chun in fact abetted them, while Ganzi Company Commander Long Zhen colluded with them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign, the Miao bandits Long Mayang of Cuoxi and Long Tongbao of Tongren gathered followers to raid and plunder. Native officials such as Li Chun abetted them, and Ganzi Company Commander Long Zhen colluded with them.

sentences.zh: 後遂四出劫掠，遠近騷然，先後守臣莫能制。

translations.literal: Afterward they ranged in all directions to plunder; near and far were in uproar, and successive frontier officials could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: They then ranged widely in raids, throwing the region into turmoil, and successive frontier officials proved unable to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 丙將討之，賊入連山深箐，為拒守計。

translations.literal: When Bing was about to suppress them, the bandits entered the deep ravines of the linked mountains to prepare a defensive stand.
translations.idiomatic: As Liu Bing prepared to suppress them, the bandits withdrew into the deep ravines of the linked mountains to make a stand.

sentences.zh: 丙率師破其數寨。

translations.literal: Bing led troops and broke several of their stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bing led troops and captured several of their stockades.

sentences.zh: 賊走據天生崖及六龍山。

translations.literal: The bandits fled and occupied Tiansheng Cliff and Liulong Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits fled and held Tiansheng Cliff and Liulong Mountain.

sentences.zh: 貴州巡撫沈林兵繼至，連攻破之。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Shen Lin of Guizhou arrived with troops in support and captured them in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Shen Lin of Guizhou arrived with reinforcements and captured both positions in succession.

sentences.zh: 前後擒童保等二百人，斬首八百九十余級。

translations.literal: Before and after, they captured Tongbao and two hundred others and took more than eight hundred ninety heads.
translations.idiomatic: In all they captured Tongbao and two hundred others and took more than eight hundred ninety heads.

sentences.zh: 都指揮潘勛又破鎮、筸諸寨，擒麻陽等百六十人，斬首級如前，余賊遠遁。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Pan Xun again broke the stockades of Zhen and Gan, captured Mayang and one hundred sixty others, took heads in number as before, and the remaining bandits fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Pan Xun then captured the stockades at Zhen and Gan, seized Mayang and one hundred sixty others, took a comparable number of heads, and the remaining bandits fled deep into the hinterland.

sentences.zh: 璽書獎勵。

translations.literal: An imperial letter rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial letter of commendation was issued.

sentences.zh: 丙操履清介，敢任事。

translations.literal: Bing in conduct was pure and upright, and dared to take on responsibilities.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bing was upright and incorruptible, and bold in shouldering responsibility.

sentences.zh: 所至嚴明，法令修舉。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he was strict and clear, and laws and ordinances were well maintained.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he was strict and clear-minded, and laws and ordinances were rigorously enforced.

sentences.zh: 遷工部右侍郎，采木入山。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Vice Minister of Works and entered the mountains to procure timber.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Vice Minister of Works and entered the mountains to procure timber.

sentences.zh: 越二載，犯風痹得疾，卒。

translations.literal: After two years he contracted wind paralysis and fell ill, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he contracted paralysis and died of the illness.

sentences.zh: 詔贈尚書，謚恭襄。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Minister and the posthumous title Gongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Minister with the posthumous name Gongxiang.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：英、景間，瓦剌逼西陲，邊圉孔棘；

translations.literal: The commentator says: Between the Ying and Jing reigns, Oirat pressed the western frontier and the border defenses were critically strained;
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: During the reigns of the Ying and Jing emperors, the Oirats pressed the western frontier and the border defenses were critically strained;

sentences.zh: 而黃蕭養、葉宗留之徒劫掠嶺南、浙、閩境上。

translations.literal: while Huang Xiaoyang, Ye Zongliu, and their kind plundered the borders of Lingnan, Zhe, and Min.
translations.idiomatic: while Huang Xiaoyang, Ye Zongliu, and their followers raided the borders of Lingnan, Zhejiang, and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 其後荊、襄流民嘯聚，則以劉通、石龍為之魁。

translations.literal: Afterward wandering people of Jing and Xiang gathered in rebellion, with Liu Tong and Shi Long as their chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Later, displaced people in Jing and Xiang rose in rebellion under the leadership of Liu Tong and Shi Long.

sentences.zh: 他若都勻、松、茂、黔、楚諸苗、瑤叛者數起。

translations.literal: Elsewhere, among Duyun, Song, Mao, Qian, Chu, and other Miao and Yao, rebels rose repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Elsewhere, Miao and Yao rebellions broke out repeatedly in Duyun, Songpan, Maozhou, Guizhou, and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 羅亨信、侯琎諸人，保固封圻，誅虓禁亂，討則有功，撫則信著，宣力封疆，無忝厥任矣。

translations.literal: Luo Hengxin, Hou Jin, and the others secured and held the frontier territories, punished the fierce and forbade disorder; in suppression they had merit, in pacification their trust was manifest—they exerted strength on the borders and did not disgrace their commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Hengxin, Hou Jin, and their colleagues held the frontiers firm, punished the violent and suppressed disorder. They succeeded in campaigns and won trust in pacification, serving the borderlands without disgracing their commissions.

sentences.zh: 孔鏞以知府服叛瑤，其才力有過人者。

translations.literal: Kong Yong, holding the rank of prefect, subdued rebellious Yao; his talent and strength surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yong subdued rebellious Yao while serving as prefect—a man whose talent and force surpassed the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 韓愈言柳中丞行事適機宜，風采可畏愛。

translations.literal: Han Yu said of Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu that in action he suited the critical moment and his bearing inspired both awe and affection.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu wrote of Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu that his actions always suited the moment and his bearing inspired both awe and affection.

sentences.zh: 不如是，惡能以有為哉。

translations.literal: Were it not so, how could one accomplish anything through action?
translations.idiomatic: Without such qualities, how could one achieve anything worth doing?
